title: Fear of God Unifies Three House Sub-Labels for “An Eternal Perspective”
summary:
Summary

Fear of God unveils “An Eternal Perspective”, uniting Collection Nine, Eternal Order and ESSENTIALS Signature.The campaign emphasizes continuity, transcending seasons and moments with a distinct American luxury vision.Eternal serves as the foundation, guiding the brand’s pursuit of timeless intention.

Fear of God has unveiled An Eternal Perspective, a campaign that brings together three distinct pillars of the house - Collection Nine, Eternal Order and ESSENTIALS Signature - under a singular, unified narrative. Rooted in the foundational principles established by founder and creative director Jerry Lorenzo, the initiative frame-shifts away from traditional, isolated seasonal drops. Instead, it presents each sub-label as part of an interconnected design continuum, articulating a refined vision of modern American luxury through quiet elegance, intentional proportion, and meticulous craftsmanship.At its foundation, Eternal serves as the guiding principle from which Fear of God creates and communicates, positioning the brand’s work as an ongoing pursuit of transcendence through intention. “An Eternal Perspective” underscores the idea that fashion is not confined to moments or trends but is instead a lasting expression of identity and vision. Available now through fearofgod.com, the campaign reinforces Jerry Lorenzo’s philosophy of building a cohesive universe where every piece, whether from Collection Nine, Eternal Order, or ESSENTIALS, exists as part of a timeless continuum.

title: Maison Margiela's REPLICA Wraps "Lazy Sunday Morning" and "Jazz Club" Scents in Newspaper Print for Its Second Holiday 2026 Offering
summary:
Summary

Maison Margiela's REPLICA line returns with the second installment of its 2026 holiday collection, led by newspaper-print editions of two signature scentsNew additions include an "Up At Dawn" hand cream and a "By the Fireplace" candle built around wintry scent storiesTwo mix-and-match coffret sets let shoppers pair a fragrance with their choice of body care

Maison Margiela's REPLICA fragrance line is expanding its 2026 holiday offering with a second wave, anchored by limited-edition versions of "Lazy Sunday Morning" and "Jazz Club." Both eau de toilettes arrive dressed in a holiday-exclusive newspaper-style print, joined by new body care, a candle, and a pair of customizable gift sets.The two returning scents are the centerpiece, each carried over in its full 100 mL format under the "PRINT SHOP" holiday design. "Lazy Sunday Morning" builds its story around a sunny Sunday in Florence, spent wrapped in freshly laundered linen sheets, and reads as fresh and clean on the skin. "Jazz Club" pulls in the opposite direction, drawing on a private New York jazz club for a warmer, spicier profile that suggests rich cocktails and mellow whiskey for a more intimate, grown-up mood.New to this wave is the "Up At Dawn" hand cream, centered on a dawn-rose scent that opens like fresh roses blooming in a mist-covered garden. The formula does functional work alongside the fragrance, using hyaluronic acid to add moisture while shea butter and almond oil guard against dryness, finishing with a light texture meant to leave hands supple rather than heavy.Rounding out the seasonal additions is the "By the Fireplace" candle, a natural fit for winter. Its scent sets the scene in midwinter Chamonix, France, capturing the crackle of a fireplace and the faint sweetness of chestnut for a warm, enclosed feel.The collection also leans into personalization through two coffret formats. The larger 30 mL Holiday Set lets shoppers choose one 30 mL fragrance from all 14 REPLICA scents, add a body care item of their choice, and take home a 1.2 mL "Jazz Club" mini and a holiday-exclusive shopper. A more compact 10 mL Holiday Set pairs a 10 mL fragrance with a hand cream, with both drawn from a choice of "Lazy Sunday Morning" or "Up At Dawn." Standalone holiday gift versions of "Lazy Sunday Morning" in eau de toilette, hand cream, and lip balm complete the range.The second wave of Maison Margiela REPLICA's 2026 holiday collection goes on sale nationwide October 22, with early availability at select stores from October 15.

summary: 今年4月、ファッションスクールの名門、ベルギーのアントワープ王立芸術アカデミーで学ぶ日本人学生 島田響さんのもとに、授業料の改定を知らせるメールが届いた。内容は2026-2027年度から、非EEA圏*出身の新入生を対象に、年間授業料を2万5000ユーロ（約465万円）へと、従来の約3倍に引き上げるという通知だった。進む学費高騰や円安の影響によって、ファッションに限らず海外で学ぶためのハードルは大きく変わりつつある。「払える人だけ」が学べる時代になりつつあるのか。FASHIONSNAPの「次世代クリエイター」特集ラストとなる本記事では、アントワープの学費高騰を起点に、ファッション教育を取り巻く現状を考える。 *EEA（欧州経済領域）は、EU加盟国にアイスランド、リヒテンシュタイン、ノルウェーを加えた地域。非EEA圏は、それ以外の国・地域を指す。*日本円は2026年8月28日時点の為替レート、1ユーロ＝185.95円で換算。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

Buffer Drags ‘Fast Times at Ridgemont High’ Into a Capsule Ruled by "No Shirts, No Shoes, No Dice"
summary:
Summary

Buffer, the label helmed by creative director Tetsu Nishiyama and operated by HUMAN MADE, has teamed with the 1982 American teen movie for a graphics-led collectionThe collaboration runs to three T-shirt styles, each filtering the film through Buffer's own design lensA set of Buffer original pieces rounds out the release, including a long-sleeve T-shirt that reworks the brand's main logo

Buffer, the brand led by creative director Tetsu Nishiyama and operated by HUMAN MADE, is releasing a collaboration collection with Fast Times at Ridgemont High, the 1982 American high-school comedy. The capsule reads the film's world through Buffer's graphic sensibility, landing as a tight run of T-shirts rather than a sprawling licensing exercise.The collaboration centers on three T-shirt designs, each taking a different route into the source material. One is handled by illustrator Naoki Shoji, who builds his piece around the movie as a motif. A second prints a run of the film's memorable scenes directly onto the shirt, leaning on recognizable imagery. The third distills the movie down to a single line, translating its emblematic rule "NO SHIRTS, NO SHOES, NO DICE" into a standalone graphic.That three-way split is where the technical intent shows. Rather than slapping a single still on a blank, Buffer treats the film as raw material to be reinterpreted, moving from illustration to photographic scene print to text-driven graphic across the set. It is a small collection built to cover distinct graphic registers instead of repeating one idea in different colors.The film crossover also fits a longer pattern for the label. Buffer has built a throughline of movie-referencing capsules, and pairing with a 1982 teen comedy slots neatly into a graphic language rooted in American pop-culture nostalgia. Fast Times at Ridgemont High carries a specific early-80s Americana that maps onto Nishiyama's ongoing interest in vintage US reference points, giving the T-shirts a cultural anchor beyond the artwork itself.Alongside the collaboration, Buffer is offering its own originals in the same drop. Those include a T-shirt drawing on 1990s street culture and a long-sleeve T-shirt that reconstructs the brand's main logo, extending the release past the film tie-in and into Buffer's core graphic identity.The Buffer x Fast Times at Ridgemont High collection releases September 5 at Buffer Store and the Buffer official online store.

Ami Paris Celebrates Friendship and Parisian Elegance for FW26 Campaign
summary:
Summary

Ami Paris debuts FW26 campaign starring brand friends like Saskia de Brauw.Key offerings span versatile outerwear, the Mirage sneaker and the crocodile-embossed Carrousel bag.Available now at Ami Paris boutiques globally and online.

For Fall/Winter 2026, Ami Paris honors the real people and longtime friends who inspire creative director Alexandre Mattiussi. Set against a clean studio backdrop to highlight both the individuals and the garments, the series of spontaneous portraits functions as a manifesto of Parisian elegance and effortless ease. The casting brings together familiar faces of the house - including Rebecca Leigh, Saskia de Brauw, George Anderson, Jia Jingwen, Dara Gueye, Mack Karpes, Elliot Belot and Mohamed Benhadda - each bringing their unique personality to showcase how inclusivity and togetherness define the brand's identity.Designed for real-life wearability, the new seasonal wardrobe emphasizes comfortable, protective and versatile silhouettes rendered in a palette of quiet neutrals and earthy tones, punctuated by deep natural colors and bright red accents. Key collection highlights include signature tailoring and seasonal outerwear, rounded out by standout accessories such as the Carrousel bag in burgundy crocodile-embossed leather, the new Mirage sneaker, and graphic baseball caps embroidered with the message: "Thank you for being a friend."The Ami Paris FW26 collection is available now at Ami Paris boutiques worldwide and online via amiparis.com.

A$AP Rocky and PUMA Turn ‘Don't Be Dumb’ Into a Man City Jersey Dropping This Weekend
summary:
Summary

A$AP Rocky and PUMA translate the visual world of his 2026 album into a limited-edition Manchester City jersey collectionA retail longsleeve in black and archive gold runs alongside a players-only gift edition built on the club's sky-blue identityThe launch lands ahead of Rocky's September 5 performance at Co-op Live, with a one-night city-centre activation kicking things off

A$AP Rocky and PUMA have linked with Manchester City on a limited-edition jersey collection that maps the rapper's 2026 album Don't Be Dumb onto club apparel. The tie-up pairs City's reinvention-driven identity with Rocky's own restless creative streak, arriving just before his September 5 show at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.The headline retail piece is a longsleeve shirt in black and archive gold. "DON'T BE DUMB" runs down the sleeve, while a bold "MANCHESTER" graphic stretches across the back, pushing the city itself to the front of the design. Fans can also add limited-edition "A$AP 11" name and number printing to their 26/27 Home, Away or Third jersey while stocks last.Running parallel is a players-only gift edition that stays closer to City's core look. It swaps the black and gold for the club's familiar sky blue, tucks subtle "D.B.D." detailing onto the sleeve, and lands a stop-sign graphic across the back reading "STOP SNITCHIN, MANCHESTER.""PUMA's got deep roots with Manchester City, and I wanted to bring my own perspective," A$AP Rocky said in the announcement. "We created something that feels true to my design language and the Don't Be Dumb ethos, while still honoring the club's legacy."The drop is Manchester-exclusive and first-come, first-served, spread across a tight sequence of windows. PUMA kicks things off Friday, September 4 by transforming Black Milk in the Northern Quarter into the "Don't Be Dumb Caff" for one night only, where the longsleeve jersey goes on sale first with doors opening at 4 p.m. The "A$AP 11" name and number becomes available that evening at the event and at the official Man City Stadium and Arndale stores. A second run of the longsleeve then hits the Stadium Store on September 5 from the 9:30 a.m. UK opening, ahead of City's Premier League clash against Coventry.Dominique Gathier, PUMA VP Teamsport, framed the project as an extension of the brand's wider ambitions. "A$AP Rocky brings a creative energy to everything he touches and this collection is a natural extension of what our partnership stands for – taking football into spaces it does not normally occupy and doing it with a level of craft and intention that feels right for both the clubs and for him."The A$AP Rocky x PUMA x Manchester City collection goes on sale exclusively in Manchester, starting September 4 at the Northern Quarter event and continuing September 5 at the Man City Stadium Store.

title: Lee Taps Nigel Cabourn’s OX’ed Silver for a 101st Anniversary Workwear Capsule
summary:
Summary

Lee and Nigel Cabourn's OX’ed Silver celebrate 101 years of "101" with a 10-piece collection.Features custom "BRURRY DENIM" recreating irregular 1920s European steam-spun yarns.Launches September 12, 2026, exclusively via Nigel Cabourn flagships and online.

To celebrate the 101st anniversary of Lee’s iconic "101" line, American heritage brand Lee has partnered with Nigel Cabourn's OX’ed Silver to release a collaborative workwear collection.Reinterpreting early 20th-century labor uniforms, the partnership introduces "BRURRY DENIM," a custom fabric engineered to mimic the irregular, uneven yarns of 1920s European underwear stock created by early steam and water-powered spinning machinery. The material utilizes three distinct dyeing techniques — hank dyeing incorporating dead-leaf tannins and iron mordanting, rope dyeing inspired by WWII-era material shortages, and cheese dyeing drawing from British Army green denim.The 10-piece collection is organized into three distinct series inspired by American occupations between the 1920s and 1940s: "Railwayman 1925–1939," "Ranch Worker 1940–1944," and "Rodeo Clown 1943–1946". The range comprises six denim styles, including modified iterations of Lee’s signature LOCO Jacket, 91-SB Overalls and 101 jeans, alongside four complementary items: a band-collar work shirt, two-pack field tees, low-back suspenders, and graphic bandanas.Priced between ¥8,250 - ¥99,000 JPY (approx. $53 - $633 USD), the Lee x Nigel Cabourn OX’ed Silver collection will officially release on September 12, 2026, and will be available exclusively through Nigel Cabourn flagship stores and the official webstore.

summary: オーセンティック・ブランズ・グループ（Authentic Brands Group、以下ABG）は、ファッションやスポーツ、エンターテインメント、キャラクターなどのブランド管理を手がける企業だ。2010年に米国で創業した同社は、「チャンピオン（Champion）」や「リーボック（Reebok）」、「ブルックス ブラザーズ（Brooks Brothers）」などのブランドや、マリリン・モンロー（Marilyn Monroe）やデビッド・ベッカム（David Beckham）、エルヴィス・プレスリー（Elvis Presley）といった著名人の商標権や知的財産（IP）を保有。各国・地域で現地市場に詳しいパートナー企業と組み、ブランド運営の実務を委託し、その対価としてロイヤリティ収入を得るビジネスモデルを展開している。現在50超のブランドを抱え、全世界における売り上げは380億ドル（約6兆859億円）、SNSでの総フォロワー数は9億8000万人を誇る。 　今回ABGは、日本での新たなパートナーシップ構築を見越し「日本市場戦略発表会」を開催した。登壇した同社のウェスリー・チュウ（Wesley Chu）APAC（アジア太平洋）プレジデントに、日本におけるブランド拡大戦略やキャラクターIPの可能性、Z世代攻略の鍵などを聞いた。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: Alpha Industries Wears Its History Well For The “RE:ISSUE” Collection
summary:
Summary

Alpha Industries' Fall/Winter 2026 "RE:ISSUE" collection introduces a new surface treatment, Battlewash, inspired by the natural aging of vintage garments.The collection centers on three iconic silhouettes: the CWU-45/P Bomber Jacket, the N-2B Parka, and the MA-1 Bomber Jacket, each reimagined with aged, distressed detailing.The Alpha Industries "RE:ISSUE" Fall/Winter 2026 collection is now available at AlphaIndustries.com, the brand's New York City flagship (290 Lafayette St., New York, NY), and select retailers worldwide.

This Fall/Winter season, Alpha Industries is honoring and reimagining their timeless military outerwear heritage through wear, texture, and finish. With a new approach to the brand’s iconic silhouettes; the CWU-45/P Bomber Jacket, the N-2B Parka, and the classic MA-1 Bomber Jacket, the “RE:ISSUE” collection introduces Battlewash, a worn-in surface treatment inspired by the natural aging of vintage military garments. Leading the collection are the CWU-45/P Bomber Jacket and N-2B Parka, both reimagined with aged treatments and distressed detailing, emphasizing their military origins through a naturally worn appearance. The iconic MA-1 Bomber Jacket follows suit, an iconic design reimagined through texture and detail. Rather than reproducing archival garments, the collection reworks and evolves familiar military silhouettes through updated surface treatments, proportions, and styling, maintaining the brand’s dedication to functionality and authenticity. Beyond the brand’s iconic outerwear, the Battlewash treatment extends to other Alpha Industries essentials, such as sweatpants and fleece, bringing the “RE:ISSUE” texture and finish across a broader range of everyday styles. The Alpha Industries "RE:ISSUE" Fall/Winter 2026 collection is now available at AlphaIndustries.com, the brand's New York City flagship (290 Lafayette St., New York, NY), and select retailers worldwide.

title: 「ユウショウコバヤシ」の過剰な少女的かわいさにはなぜ中毒性があるのか？　27年春夏
summary: TikTokやInstagramを見ていると、「流行」よりも、アルゴリズムによって細かく分かれた「界隈」の情報を目にすることが増えたように感じる。かつてテレビや雑誌が機能していた時代に作られた大衆向けの「トレンド」という言葉は、以前ほど大きな力を持たなくなった。誰もが同じものを見るのではなく、個人の関心に合わせて情報が届くようになったことで、流行もそれぞれのコミュニティの中で生まれるようになったという解釈が正しいのだろう。 　この視点から「ユウショウコバヤシ（yushokobayashi）」を観察すると、とても興味深い。2026年秋冬シーズンに東京ファッションウィークの公式スケジュールへ初参加し、今回で2度目となるこのブランドの凄さは、その「コミュニティ」にある。ショー会場に集まるファンは、ブランドの服で全身を固めている人はもちろんのこと、そうでなくともパステルカラー、フリル、手編みのニットといった「共通言語」を身に纏っている。一言で表すならば、過剰なほどの「少女的かわいい」。ここに足を運ぶ人々は、自分の中にある少女を否定しなくていい場所を共有しているように感じる。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: RequaL≡ 2027SS コレクション
summary: 土居哲也が手掛ける「リコール（RequaL≡）」が、「Rakuten Fashion Week TOKYO 2027 S/S」でランウェイショーを開催し、2027年春夏コレクションを発表した。会場は渋谷ヒカリエホールA。 　今季のテーマは、“記憶とコードを書き換える”という概念を着想源にした「（re）codex（re）member」。ブランドが歩んできた10年間を振り返りながら、過去の記憶と衣服にまつわる既成概念を“書き換える”ことを試みた。 　ショーは、ヴァイオリニストの岩住励によるどこか不穏な生演奏とともに幕を開けた。2枚のシャツをドッキングして一着に仕立てたファーストルックを皮切りに、衣服の固定観念をひっくり返す、通称「反転劇」を取り入れたルックが次々と登場。複数のシャツの身頃をつなぎ合わせたスカートや、シャツを上下逆さにしてサルエルパンツに落とし込んだボトムス、ランプシェードに見立てた帽子など、既存のアイテムを解体し、本来とは異なる役割を与えることで新たなシルエットを提案した。 　再構築の対象は衣服だけではなく、土居自身の記憶にも及んだ。幼少期に遊んでいたぬいぐるみを取り付けたベストが登場したほか、過去のコレクションで発表したクマのモチーフを、衣装制作などを手掛けるブランド「もりもり（mori mori）」との協業で再解釈。ブラウンとアイボリーを基調に、全身を細かなフリルで覆ったドリーミーな一着へと生まれ変わらせた。今季はもりもりのほか、「バナル シック ビザール（banal chic bizarre）」や「ケイスケヨシダ（KEISUKEYOSHIDA）」「ニューローズ（NewRose）」「オーバーレース（overlace）」「再倖築」など11組のブランドやクリエイターと協業。土居がかつて憧れた先輩から、ともに歩んできた仲間、リコールを見て成長してきた次世代まで、それぞれとのコラボレーションを通じてブランドの過去、現在、未来を一つのランウェイに重ね合わせた。 　リコールがランウェイ形式でコレクションを発表するのは約3年ぶり。土居はその間、「リコールに求められているものと、自分が表現したいこと」の間で揺れながら、「見せる服」と「着せる服」のあり方を模索してきたという。今回のショーでは、そうした葛藤を経て、自身の生活や記憶、過去に生み出したアイデア、これまで築いてきた人々とのつながりを改めてクリエイションへと昇華。11年目以降は「見せる服」と「着せる服」の双方をアップデートしながら、流行に迎合することなく、自身のペースでブランドを続けていきたいと語った。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: The Airport Runway Becomes a Surreal Backdrop for Jil Sander’s FW26 Campaign
summary:
Jil Sander has unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 campaign, crafted under the creative direction of Simone Bellotti. Shot on the open tarmac of a private airport runway by photographer and videographer Moni Haworth, the visual narrative presents a surreal, outdoor interior setup featuring foil-wrapped sofas and latex-covered tables.Starring models Edie Campbell and Daisuke Ueda, the campaign embraces grainy VHS textures, desaturated hues, and a cinematic tension echoing the styles of Hitchcock and Fassbinder. Anchored by the score "If This Is Hell” by Space Afrika featuring Deuén, the campaign channels an unsettling yet elegant atmosphere, charged with what Bellotti describes as “erotic electricity.” The juxtaposition of minimalism and excess, of addition and subtraction, defines the season’s mood — an abstract story where beauty lies in contradiction.The featured seasonal lineup twists Jil Sander's signature stripped-back minimalism through a framework of heightened restraint and subtle contradiction. The collection focuses on precise, abridged silhouettes where the superfluous is stripped away to highlight pure essential form. Tailored outerwear, structured separates, and refined daily wardrobe staples balance a sense of powerful simplicity with unexpected textural elements. Check out the accompanying campaign film below. title: Hong Kong Palace Museum Transforms Into a Haute Couture Stage for “VIRTUOSE”
summary:
Summary

HKFDA presented VIRTUOSE: The Artistry of Couture 2026 at the Hong Kong Palace Museum, launching the third Hong Kong Fashion Fest.The event showcased 40 custom looks from haute couture houses, spanning Guillermo Décimo, Phan Huy, Tigerstrolling Artisanal and Vivian Luk Atelier.

Presented by the Hong Kong Fashion Designers Association (HKFDA) and sponsored by the Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency (CCIDA), the flagship VIRTUOSE: The Artistry of Couture 2026 event took place yesterday at the Hong Kong Palace Museum. Serving as the official opening event for the third annual Hong Kong Fashion Fest, the immersive showcase transformed the museum into a cross-cultural stage framed by four architectural arches — ranging from a traditional Chinese courtyard to neoclassical and Franco-Vietnamese designs. Designed to solidify Hong Kong’s position as an international hub for haute couture, the event attracted global fashion figures, industry leaders and local celebrities including Louise Wong  Susie Lau, Irene Kim and Hanan Besovic.The runway presentations brought together four emerging and established couture brands from Hong Kong, Spain and Vietnam, delivering a collective showing of 40 bespoke looks worn by international supermodel Christina Chung and a diverse cast. Representing Spain, Guillermo Décimo - led by Guillermo Díez López, who refined his techniques at the Museo Balenciaga - presented hand-crafted creations celebrating theatricality, heritage and slow fashion. Vietnam’s Phan Huy, who recently made history as the youngest Vietnamese designer on the official Paris Haute Couture Week calendar, showcased intricate silk weaving, traditional hand-embroidery, and modern 3D draping.Rounding out the lineup were two Hong Kong-based labels offering distinct interpretations of modern couture. Tigerstrolling Artisanal, founded in 2025 by Tiger Chung (Chung Tsz-ho and Chung Ka-ching), delivered deconstructed tailoring, unconventional proportions, and upcycled materials that bridged everyday object subversion with high-fashion technique. Meanwhile, Vivian Luk Atelier - founded by former Vera Wang designer Vivian Luk - focused on sculptural fluidity, incorporating hidden corset boning, precision bias cuts, and structured fabrications built for bespoke client styling. Following the runway shows, the event transitions to an exclusive private ordering exhibition today at The Four Seasons Hotel in Central, providing private clients and media an intimate opportunity to acquire the collection pieces.

PORTER Is Back in NYC With a Five-Day Pop-Up
summary:
Summary

YOSHIDA & Co. has opened a five-day PORTER LIMITED STORE in New York's SOHO neighborhoodThe lineup spans the house's PORTER, POTR and L.L. labels, including the MONOCHROME backpack, the RIDE series and Aurel Schmidt and HELLO KITTY collaborationsEvery bag on display is crafted and sewn in Japan, shown alongside original fixtures built specifically for the space

PORTER has returned to New York with the PORTER LIMITED STORE, a five-day pop-up from parent company YOSHIDA & Co. that puts the brand's Made-in-Japan construction on full view. Marking the label's first NYC appearance in a year, the temporary shop pulls together current collections from three of the company's brands under one roof.The selection leans into the range of YOSHIDA & Co.'s catalog. From the core PORTER line, the store carries the MONOCHROME backpack and the VINIL shoulder bag, while the POTR label brings its RIDE series across nine separate pieces. The L.L. brand rounds out the assortment with three distinct silhouettes: the OLDNEW shoulder bag, the TRUE BLUE flap shoulder bag and the FILAMENT vertical tote.Collaborative work sits alongside the mainline goods. The pop-up stocks the Aurel Schmidt x PORTER capsule and a HELLO KITTY x PORTER range that stretches across backpacks and smaller carry pieces. Each item reflects the same production standard the brand is known for, hand-assembled and sewn by Japanese artisans, a process rooted in the company's more-than-90-year history. That craftsmanship extends to the fixtures themselves, with original in-store displays designed specifically for the New York space.Beyond the bags, the store offers the recently released official visual book, YOSHIDA & Co. 90 Anniversary BOOK, available in both a Collectors Edition and a Library Edition. A selection of special items available exclusively at select locations rounds out what's on the floor.The PORTER LIMITED STORE runs until September 6 at 21 Spring Street in SOHO, on the corner of Spring and Elizabeth St.PORTER LIMITED STORE21 Spring StreetNew York

title: yushokobayashi 2027SS コレクション
summary: 今季から小林裕翔と上原碧海のデザイナー2人体制となった「ユウショウコバヤシ（yushokobayashi）」が、「Rakuten Fashion Week TOKYO 2027 S/S」でランウェイショーを開催し、2027年春夏コレクションを発表した。 　今季のテーマは、人魚姫の物語から着想した「Mermaid Tears」。昨年、ファッションアワードを受賞した際、知人に「裕翔くんはずっと地下にいると思っていた」と言われた経験を起点に、これまで自分たちがいた場所を“海の底”に重ね、地上の世界に憧れる人魚の姿を描いた。プレスリリースには「私は何と引き換えに、地上に上がれるのだろうか」と綴り、憧れた姿を手にする代わりに、喪失や痛みを知る人魚姫の物語に自身の現在地を投影した。 　コレクションでは、海の底から水面を見上げたときに差し込む光をイメージし、ホワイトや淡いブルー、ピンクを中心とした柔らかなカラーパレットを採用。ブランドを象徴するニットアイテムは、春夏シーズンらしくコットンを用いて軽やかにデザイン。立体的なカッティングも取り入れ、柔らかな素材とのコントラストを生み出した。また、花や動物、楽器などを手描きした「塗り絵」のモチーフを随所にあしらい、一部にはデザイナー自身が手作業で着色。「自分で色を付ける」という行為に、まだ見ぬ地上の世界への憧れを重ねた。 　ショーの終盤では、地上への憧れから、その先で知る痛みへと物語が展開。フィナーレではモデルの一人が靴を脱ぎ、人間の足を得る代わりに一歩ごとに痛みを味わう人魚姫の姿を表現し、地上へ出ることで得た自由と、その代償を描き出した。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: Diesel Ships Life-Sized Cardboard Cutouts Worldwide for FW26 “Multiplicities” Campaign
summary:
Summary

Diesel FW26 “Multiplicities” campaign spans global cities, reframing visuals through local perspectives.Spotlighted styles include the D‑ONE bag, 3‑D Denim, and Cut Out Floral Knits.Available across DIESEL stores and online.

Diesel has unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 campaign, titled "Multiplicities," presenting a collaborative world tour that redefines traditional global fashion imagery. Conceived by creative director Glenn Martens and art director Christopher Simmonds, the campaign begins in the studio before cardboard cutouts of models are shipped worldwide. Local photographers in cities from London to New Delhi reinterpret the imagery, embedding their own perspectives and environments into the narrative, transforming static visuals into a living, collaborative story.Across each stop, the campaign highlights key FW26 styles in context. In London, accessories like the D‑ONE bag and D‑COCCO stiletto sandal appear among the bustle of Piccadilly Circus. Shanghai introduces 3‑D Denim and Bicolor Leather, while Cairo sets Wrinkled Boiled Knitwear against the pyramids. Rio brings Concert Print Ts and the Stinger Watch to Ipanema’s beaches, and New Delhi showcases Cut Out Floral Knits and trompe l’oeil cable knit denim amid rickshaw tours.Anchoring the season is the D‑ONE bag, Diesel’s new signature accessory, designed with a slouchy leather silhouette and buckled straps inspired by worn belts sliding through denim loops. Available in treated leather and patchwork variations, the D‑ONE embodies versatility and global appeal.Explore the full FW26 collection through Diesel's official website and flagships around the world.

title: Public School Reclaims NYC for FW26 Campaign
summary:
SummaryPublic School's "The City Is Mine" FW26 campaign highlights NYC's influence with versatile, tailored outerwear shot by Joshua Woods.Emphasizing New York's cultural attitude, the label will debut its SS27 collection at NYFW on September 10, 2026.Following up on their big return to NYFW in early 2026, Public School has now unveiled its FW26 campaign, “The City Is Mine.” Through a nocturnal photo series, the campaign traverses the places that have defined Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne’s label, from the neon-lit streets of Manhattan to the feet of the Brooklyn Bridge.Shot by Joshua Woods and featuring Scott Barnhill, MJ Marte, and Idriys Ali-Chow, the photos showcase some of the standout pieces from the collection. Statement outerwear focuses on trench silhouettes, including a sleek black leather overcoat and a belted gray tweed coat, flowing in the breeze. For tailoring, a minimal black suit, worn by Idriys, is styled with a sepia-toned graphic button-up, while a black jacket, worn by Scott, features a toggled standing collar.Heavily shaped by its NYC provenance, Public School continues to look to the city’s diverse culture and the versatile ways of dressing across communities. Their latest collection combines influences from tailoring, sportswear, and streetwear, rooted in the movement between differing environments and expressions of style across the five boroughs. In Public School’s recent digital cover story for Hypebeast, Dao Yi-Chow reflected on how NYC continues to push their direction, “When we talk about our version of New York, it always comes back to the same things: ease, a high taste level that comes from exposure to so many different cultures, versatility, and modularity.” “The universal idea of New York isn’t necessarily about the clothes you wear. It’s about how you wear them. It’s the attitude,” Dao added.As the SS27 season approaches, Public School is set to present its next collection at NYFW on September 10, 2026.

title: EITARO 2027SS コレクション
summary: 上村英太郎が手掛ける「エイタロー（EITARO）」が、「Rakuten Fashion Week TOKYO 2027 S/S」に参加し、2027年春夏コレクションをランウェイショー形式で発表した。会場は渋谷ヒカリエのホールB。 　デビュー3シーズン目となる今季のテーマは「脱」。過去の自分を捨てて生まれ変わる「脱却」や「脱皮」をインスピレーション源に、自身の過去との向き合い方をコレクションへと落とし込んだ。「黒歴史と呼ばれるような過去も、赤や青、黄色といったさまざまな記憶が重なることで黒く見えているだけであり、一つひとつを振り返れば色鮮やかなものなのではないか」とショーを終えた上村。過去を否定するのではなく、その中にある色に気づくことを「脱」と捉え、ルックはあえて黒を使わずに製作したという。 　コレクションは、空気をはらむ軽やかなシルエットが印象的なオールホワイトのルックでスタート。初めて取り入れたという透け感のあるオーガンジーを幾重にも重ね、白一色の中に濃淡と奥行きを生み出した。続くルックでは、赤と青を重ねて紫、赤と黄色を重ねてオレンジを表現するなど、生地の重なりによる多彩な色彩を表現。このほか、ドットやチェックといった柄を取り入れ、コレクションに視覚的な変化を加えた。 　ショーの終盤では、上村自身が綴った詩を友人が朗読する音声が会場に流され、赤、青、黄色の長いオーガンジーを幾重にも重ねることで黒に近い色を生み出したルックがゆっくりとした歩みで登場。「過去は色鮮やかな記憶の重なり」というデザイナーの考えを象徴的に示した。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: 8 Drops You Don't Want to Miss This Week
summary:
With another week upon us, we have yet another installment of our product drops series.This week’s lineup of drops kicks off with Supreme honoring Larry Clark’s legendary Tulsa archive through a photography-driven Fall 2026 collaboration, while Palace Skateboards balances stormproof GORE-TEX outerwear with pitch-ready sportswear for its fifth seasonal delivery. Global pop icon JENNIE makes her official co-design debut with adidas Originals on the ballet-infused "FUNCTIONAL GRACE" collection, just as Travis Scott’s Cactus Jack and Nike serve up the rebellious, tennis-themed "Cactus Court" capsule following its US Open debut. Parisian label côte&ciel blurs the line between luggage and wearable garments with its origami-like FW26 collection, while sacai stages an immersive "sacai TO GO" pop-up at Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche featuring exclusive merchandise co-curated by Sarah Andelman. PLEASURES and Umbro team up to filter classic football heritage through a 1990s Britpop lens, and closing out the week, Denim Tears taps Billionaire Boys Club for the second installment of Tremaine Emory’s André Leon Talley-inspired collection.Check out this week’s 8 drops you don’t want to miss below.Supreme x Larry Clark Collaboration Supreme has officially partnered with celebrated American photographer and film director Larry Clark for a Fall 2026 collaborative release that honors his influential Tulsa legacy. Translating Clark's storied photographic archive into a focused range of streetwear, the capsule features original imagery alongside new, exclusive photographs across graphic apparel. Standout items include a Hooded Varsity Jacket decorated with full-placement photography, a Sequin Raglan Long-Sleeve Top, and candid portrait graphic tees. Extending beyond apparel, the collection incorporates curated lifestyle goods, a co-branded skateboard deck, and a collectible 48-page zine featuring an exclusive poster insert. The Supreme x Larry Clark Fall 2026 collaboration releases globally on September 3 through Supreme’s physical chapter locations and online store, followed by an Asia drop on September 5.Palace Fall 2026 Drop 5Palace Skateboards continues its Fall 2026 rollout with Drop 5, balancing heavy technical outerwear with a strong run of sports-referencing apparel. The undisputed centerpiece of the collection is a stormproof GORE-TEX jacket, arriving in four versatile colorways with matching hats. The performance-driven theme extends into warming Polartec fleeces detailed with reflective strips and Velcro Tri-Ferg accents. Running alongside the utilitarian outerwear is a robust sportswear current featuring mesh team jerseys with custom name tapes, as well as Palermo-inspired rugby tops and training sweats that pull directly from classic pitch traditions. Palace’s Fall 2026 Drop 5 launches in-store and online on September 4 for the UK, Europe, and the US, followed by a September 5 release in Japan, China, Korea, and Australia.adidas Originals by JENNIE “FUNCTIONAL GRACE” Collection Marking her transition from brand ambassador to true co-designer, global pop icon JENNIE has teamed up with adidas Originals for her debut "FUNCTIONAL GRACE" Fall/Winter 2026 collection. The partnership reinterprets traditional athletic codes by infusing foundational ballet elements into a surreal, futuristic vision of modern femininity. At the center of the drop is the highly anticipated SUPERSTAR SQ BALLET, a dramatic, square-toed redesign of the classic shell-toe crafted with premium leather and soft lambskin lining. The accompanying apparel expands the narrative through elevated, modular wardrobe staples, including wraparound track tops, sheer bodysuits, wrap skirts, and polar fleece hoodies, rounded out by high-knit leg warmers. The adidas Originals by JENNIE "FUNCTIONAL GRACE" collection officially releases globally on September 1 via adidas.Cactus Jack x Nike "Cactus Court" CollectionAfter tennis phenom Carlos Alcaraz was spotted at the US Open sporting new Travis Scott Nikes, Cactus Jack officially dropped the expansive "Cactus Court" collection. Merging La Flame's signature Houston streetwear aesthetic with classic tennis club traditions, the collaboration delivers a fresh take on court-ready performance and lifestyle apparel. The collection seamlessly blends country club heritage with modern, rebellious graphics across a range of co-branded athletic wear, accessories, and signature footwear styles. Designed for both the grandstand and the streets, the Cactus Jack x Nike "Cactus Court" collection is available now exclusively through Travis Scott's official webstore.côte&ciel FW26 CollectionParisian bag and accessories brand côte&ciel explores fashion as an active, transformative verb for its Fall/Winter 2026 collection. Directed by Emilie Arnault and inspired by European folk festival costumes, the seasonal range evolves the label's iconic silhouettes through fluid, body-responsive forms that bridge the gap between carrying goods and wearable garments. The origami-like construction highlights key pieces such as the expanding ELVO backpack, the RENO shoulder bag that unfolds into a hooded vest, and the versatile PO S nylon sling. Finished in an earthy, tactile palette of tweeds and technical fabrics, the côte&ciel FW26 collection is available now globally through the brand's official channels and will be stocked by HBX starting September 2.sacai TO GO MerchJapanese luxury label sacai is staging a limited-time immersive pop-up titled "sacai TO GO" inside Paris's Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche. Part of the department store's SUPER JAPON program, the takeover—co-curated by former colette Creative Director Sarah Andelman—blends Japanese culture with Parisian creativity through an exclusive roster of highly coveted merchandise. The eclectic product range includes collaborative T-shirts, Zantan tote bags crafted from repurposed archival fabrics, plush key charms by Peloqoon, and a playful magnetic RYVDOLL paper-doll set. Accompanied by a rotating weekend lineup of Japanese confectioners and Paris coffee shops, the "sacai TO GO" event and its exclusive merchandise are available now at Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche, running through October 11.PLEASURES x Umbro Capsule CollectionLos Angeles streetwear imprint PLEASURES and classic sportswear brand Umbro have joined forces to filter football heritage through the lens of 1990s Britpop. Drawing direct inspiration from the understated, rebellious style of British youth culture icons like Damon Albarn and Liam Gallagher, the capsule revives the moment when oversized football shirts, track jackets, and training gear effortlessly crossed over from the terraces into everyday gig wardrobes. The collection strips classic athletic kits of their matchday context, framing the retro-sportswear pieces as unbothered, casual staples rooted deeply in music and subculture. The PLEASURES x Umbro Britpop football collaboration drops globally on September 4 via PLEASURES and select retailers.PLEASURESDenim Tears x Billionaire Boys Club CollaborationAs the second installment of Tremaine Emory’s Fall/Winter 2026 André Leon Talley-inspired collection, Denim Tears has launched an official collaboration with Billionaire Boys Club. Fronted by rapper Peezy in a New York City-shot lookbook, the drop honors Talley’s legacy of championing Black fashion designers and effortlessly mixing diaspora clothing with traditional luxury. Standout pieces include a chunky, full-zip knit cardigan featuring BBC branding and Denim Tears' signature Pan-African striping, alongside a vibrant red bandana-patterned PrimaLoft puffer decorated with Cotton Wreath insignias. The Denim Tears x Billionaire Boys Club FW26 drop officially releases on September 4 at 11 AM ESTonline, in-store at African Diaspora Goods, and at the brand's Atlanta residency.

title: Thom Browne Captures Quiet, Melancholic Scottish Elegance in Its Fall 2026 Campaign
summary:
Summary

Thom Browne unveils its Fall 2026 collection campaign, titled "homeward...," shot by Robbie Lawrence in Birnam, Scotland.Key pieces feature Fair Isle cashmere knits, pearl-embellished tailoring and down-filled windowpane tweed outerwear.The collection is available now.

Thom Browne has unveiled its Fall 2026 campaign, titled "homeward…", photographed by Robbie Lawrence in and around Birnam, Scotland. Shot across rolling meadows and hillside towns featuring a cast of local residents and brand friends, the visual narrative honors the American designer's long-standing connection to traditional Scottish textile craftsmanship — including his officially registered grey and navy tartan developed with Loch Carron.Grounded in centuries of artisanal weaving knowledge and local raw materials, the seasonal collection highlights a rich array of knitwear, sportswear-infused technical outerwear and reinterpreted formalwear. The knitwear range utilizes time-honored techniques across fine cashmere and merino wool, executing cable-knit constructions, complex jacquards, Fair Isle patterning, and graphic intarsia motifs. These appear across relaxed and classic V-neck pullovers, cardigans, and exaggerated patchwork pieces.Bridging high-performance utility with formal tailoring, new outerwear silhouettes combine technical downfill with suiting fabrics such as chalk stripe flannel, jacket-weight cashmere, and windowpane tweed. Functional ski-inspired details - including engineered thumbholes and rib-knit gaiters - are integrated directly into cropped zip-front vests, football parkas, and low calf-length jackets.Reinterpreting black-tie codes, the collection expands formal silhouettes into sharp dresses, capes, and structured sport coats. Traditional tailoring conventions are subverted using trompe l'oeil detailing and open-back apron closures, while classic windowpane checks are rendered in precise grids of pearls. The Thom Browne Fall 2026 collection is available now globally via thombrowne.com, Thom Browne standalone flagships, and select luxury wholesale stockists.

title: Peezy Previews Denim Tears x Billionaire Boys Club Collaboration
summary:
At the top of August, Denim Tears presented a full-fledged, 153-piece Fall/Winter 2026 collection inspired by André Leon Talley, historically marking the first-ever authorized apparel collaboration to come from the editor's estate. Since its reveal, Tremaine Emory's imprint has slowly begun rolling out the seasonal range for purchase, now preparing to release the second installment — complete with a brand-new Peezy-fronted lookbook.Fresh off a new MOWALOLA teaser and the Slime Language 3 album, the Øway rapper poses in a selection of Denim Tears collection on the streets of New York City. He's seen wearing the Denim Tears x Billionaire Boys Club collaboration, featuring a chunky, full-zip knit cardigan sweater with BBC branding across the middle and Denim Tears' classic red, black, and green striping on the left upper arm."This Fall/Winter is an exploration of a specific part of André Leon Talley’s style that had social implications within and beyond fashion," Emory said in a statement when the full collection lookbook dropped."André was the first in fashion to herald Black fashion designers such as Phat Farm, Billionaire Boys Club, Dapper Dan, etc, showing up front row at shows and wearing their clothes at a time when no one else did in the fashion world. This collection will focus on the mix of diaspora clothing, Black designers, and traditional fashion that he mixed effortlessly."The bandana-patterned, PrimaLoft-filled down puffer is also a standout piece, dipped in a bright red hue, and finished off with white Cotton Wreath insignias throughout. The Wreath also lands on two new sweat sets (in navy blue and pink), as well as all over a sleek, all-black PrimaLoft-filled down vest.Take a closer look in the lookbook above and cop a piece this Friday, September 4 at 11 AM EST online, in-store at African Diaspora Goods, and at the Atlanta residency in Lenox Square.

title: Albino & Preto x atmos x ASICS Charge the GEL-Kayano 12.1 With Volt-Inspired Energy
summary:
Name: Albino & Preto x atmos x ASICS GEL-Kayano 12Colorway: Black/Safety Yellow, White/Safety YellowSKU: 1203B227-100, 1203B227-001MSRP: TBCRelease Date: September 4, September 6 (online)Where to Buy: JJCON, Albino & PretoAlbino & Preto, ASICS and atmos have linked on a three-way collaboration anchored by the GEL-Kayano 12.1, the retro-lifestyle runner reworked here with a distinctly athletic edge. Drawing on the energy of the Volt colorway, the project leans into a vibrant, performance-minded color story rather than a subdued lifestyle palette.The footwear arrives in two distinct colorways, each built around the same design logic. Fluorescent highlights supply the high-visibility punch that ties the look back to its Volt inspiration, while reflective overlays add a technical, light-catching layer across the upper. The result reads as competitive and motion-driven, a palette meant to evoke performance in progress rather than sit still on a shelf. Underpinning the aesthetics is ASICS' signature GEL cushioning, the technology that gives the Kayano line its reputation for reliable, versatile support and keeps this build functional as well as loud.Complementing the shoes, A&P and atmos put together a coordinated mesh apparel kit designed to move as easily as the footwear. The kit centers on performance mesh shorts and a matching polo, built for breathability and range of motion. Its intended use is deliberately broad, engineered to carry from no-gi jiu-jitsu training and soccer matches through to something as low-key as a trip to the local farmers market. That versatility is the throughline: gear that reads as athletic but slots into everyday wear without missing a beat.The collection drops in person at JJCON on September 4 before releasing online September 6 at 9 a.m. exclusively via A&P online. The coordinated mesh apparel kit will be available exclusively in the US market.

title: PLEASURES and Umbro Revisit '90s British Terrace Style in a New Capsule Collection
summary:
Summary

PLEASURES has teamed with Umbro on a capsule collection that reframes the sportswear brand's football roots through 1990s British music cultureThe range spans football shirts, track jackets, training pieces and sportswear, drawing on the era when kit and casualwear became one and the sameIts reference points are the wardrobes of Blur’s Damon Albarn and Oasis’ Liam Gallagher, two faces of the decade's football-meets-music attitude

PLEASURES and Umbro have joined forces on a capsule collection that reads Umbro's football history through a distinctly musical lens. Built around the crossover of sport, sound and style that defined 1990s Britain, the collaboration looks back to a moment when a football shirt was as likely to turn up at a gig as on the terraces.The collection pulls from classic Umbro product, revisiting the point in the '90s when football shirts, track jackets, training gear and general sportswear slipped effortlessly into everyday dress. That blurring is the whole premise: kit stripped of its matchday context and absorbed into a broader wardrobe, worn less for allegiance than for how it looked and felt. PLEASURES leans into that idea rather than treating it as nostalgia, framing the pieces as everyday staples first.The tonal anchor is the dress sense of Blur’s Damon Albarn and Oasis’ Liam Gallagher, two figures the release positions as shorthand for the understated, rebellious streak of '90s British youth culture. Their look, all oversized silhouettes, vintage sportswear and loose, casual layering, sat squarely at the intersection of football, music and streetwear, and it is that unbothered attitude, the sense of wearing something simply because it clicked, that the capsule sets out to capture.For PLEASURES, the pairing is a natural fit. The Los Angeles label has built its identity on music-rooted references, and channeling Umbro's heritage through the terrace-and-gig culture of the era lets both names play to their strengths. The result is less a straight football drop than a study of how sport and subculture dressed alike for a brief, influential window.The PLEASURES x Umbro capsule collection drops Friday, September 4 PLEASURES and select retailers.

title: Carlos Sainz and New Era Launch the Debut "TEAM FIFTY5" Headwear and Apparel Collection
summary:
Summary

New Era has teamed with Formula 1 driver Carlos Sainz for TEAM FIFTY5, a debut headwear and apparel collection shaped by his personal styleThe Fall/Holiday 2026 range spans 9TWENTY, 9FORTY and 9FORTY A-Frame caps plus hoodies and T-shirts in a muted palette accented by a red chili-pepper motifA standout yellow 9FORTY cap nods to Sainz's home race in Madrid, tying the launch to his fan community at the track

New Era and Carlos Sainz have introduced TEAM FIFTY5, the first headwear and apparel collection from the Formula 1 driver's community brand. Built around Sainz's own aesthetic, the debut range carries the identity of TEAM FIFTY5, named after his car number, off the racetrack and into an everyday wardrobe.The product mix leans on New Era's core headwear vocabulary. Caps arrive across the 9TWENTY, 9FORTY and 9FORTY A-Frame silhouettes, giving the collection a spread from structured to relaxed fits, while the apparel side covers loose and oversized T-shirts and hoodies alongside slim and cropped women's tees. Detailing is where the personal touches land: select pieces feature direct embroidery and a woven red chili pepper, a reference to Sainz's "Chili" nickname that doubles as the emblem of the TEAM FIFTY5 community.The palette keeps things deliberately understated, running through outdoor green, off-white, white, faded blue and red, in line with a creative direction the brand roots in elevated essentials and European heritage. The intent is a set of pieces that reads as considered and versatile rather than loudly branded motorsport merchandise, wearable well beyond a race weekend. Against that restrained backdrop, one piece breaks from the muted tone: a yellow 9FORTY cap with red details, created for fans in the TEAM FIFTY5 Grandstand at Sainz's home race in Madrid. The color pulls from one of the driver's favorites while nodding to the yellow of the Spanish flag, positioning it as the collection's most overtly personal design.That balance between product and personal narrative is the point of the collaboration. For Sainz, the collection is a way to extend a fan community he has built over his career into something tangible and everyday. "TEAM FIFTY5 is part of who I am since the beginning of my career," he said. "With this collection, we wanted to create something that feels authentic to that identity but can be worn every day. New Era understands the connection between sport, culture and personal style, and I'm proud of what we have created together." New Era, for its part, frames the tie-up as a natural extension of its own territory. Patrik Söderström, New Era VP EMEA, described TEAM FIFTY5 as "a natural meeting point between elite motorsport and contemporary lifestyle," created in close collaboration with Sainz and his team while staying true to the brand's heritage in headwear, sport and culture.Reinforcing that off-track positioning, the launch campaign was shot in Mallorca during the summer break, featuring Sainz and his team away from the paddock. It is a framing that treats the collection less as trackside merch and more as a lifestyle line with its own identity.The TEAM FIFTY5 collection will be available through New Era and Carlos Sainz's online channels, the New Era Madrid store at Gran Via 15, and select wholesale partners.

title: Skepta Wore Stone Island on Stage All Weekend
summary:
Skepta fronting Stone Island's latest "Community as a Form of Research" campaign ultimately comes as no surprise, as  Skepta and Stone Island have been overly locked in this year. Big Smoke has repped the brand pretty consistently throughout his summer run of shows, donning a range of the label's jacketing silhouettes for his guest appearances and solo shows alike.This past weekend — one of the U.K.'s biggest music weekends of the year — was no exception, with the rapper performing at England's Reading & Leeds 2027, as well as Ireland's Electric Picnic, and wearing a different Stone Island piece for each set.Friday, Skepta took the stage at Reading, where he wore the centerfold piece of the weekend. Lifted from the label's Spring/Summer 2001 collection, Smoke flexed a highly coveted archival jacket silhouette: the Stone Island Micro Felt Transparent Cover Jacket. Designed by Paul Harvey during his time at the brand, the green zip-up is defined by its crumpled, paper-like appearance, a byproduct of its extremely lightweight microfelt nylon body, fully laminated with a transparent polyurethane film.The next day, the rapper graced The Grid stage at Leeds for another high-octane set, in another aptly high-octane Stone Island look. This go-around, Skepta opted for a vibrant, bright orange hooded jacket from the brand, complete with flaps on the ears and patches on the sleeves.On Sunday, he closed out the weekend a little further west, heading over to Laois, Ireland to wrap the Electric Picnic festival in a sleek Stone Island hooded rain jacket.Fast forward just a few days after Big Smoke's commendable three-day, hometown run of shows, Stone Island lifted the veil on the latest installment of its "Community as a Form of Research" portrait series, starring none other than fakemink, Stephen Graham, and, you guessed it, Skepta himself.

title: Maison Francis Kurkdjian Translates Desert Sand Dunes Into “OUD velvet mood” Extrait de parfum
summary:
Summary

Maison Francis Kurkdjian debuts OUD velvet mood Extrait de parfum, inspired by desert dunes and velvet’s tactile softness.The scent pairs raw oud wood with textured peach, osmanthus and a supple suede accord.Available starting today in 35ml and 70ml sizes.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian expands its iconic fabric-inspired fragrance wardrobe with "OUD velvet mood” Extrait de parfum, capturing the carnal softness of velvet through a refined, contemporary lens.Drawing inspiration from a night spent among the shifting, sun-warmed dunes of Liwa in the Persian Gulf, perfumer Francis Kurkdjian translated the tactile sensuality of desert sand into an enveloping olfactory caress. The composition builds a bridge between Eastern heritage and French perfumery by pairing the untamed, animalic richness of raw oud wood with a joyful, textured peach note. Complemented by the leathery, apricot facets of osmanthus and a supple suede accord, the fragrance creates an intimate "bare skin" effect — evoking a mood of quiet opulence, vast horizons, and lingering warmth.Reflecting the dark, mysterious depths of the scent, the bottle is crafted in a signature square silhouette made of dark, tinted crystal with sharply cut facets. To complete the visual narrative of "dark as night, bright as gold," the bottle is topped with an architectural, gold-toned cap and stamped with the house’s double "K" monogram seal embedded directly into the glass. This play of radiance and shadow mirrors the contrast between the deep, smoky resin and the luminous, velvety fruit notes within.Launching as an Extrait de parfum, which is considered by Kurkdjian to be the ultimate quintessence of fragrance concentration, the release is available in 35ml and 70ml sizes. Priced at £225 GBP (approx. $305 USD) for 35ml and £360 GBP (approx. $487 USD) for 70ml, the "OUD velvet mood” remains exclusive to Harrods Knightsbridge and H Beauty stores in the UK, while also being available through Maison Francis Kurkdjian boutiques and online flagships.

title: 三陽商会 平林義規新社長に聞く　“アパレル非専門家”が手掛ける継承と変革
summary: 三陽商会が、大きな転換期を迎えている。「バーバリー（BURBERRY）」との契約終了に伴う“バーバリーショック”から経営を立て直し、7期ぶりの営業黒字化に導いた大江伸治氏が代表取締役社長を退任。後任として代表取締役社長に就任したのは、大江氏と同じく三井物産出身で、2025年度は社外取締役として三陽商会を支えた平林義規氏だ。大江氏が代表取締役会長にとどまる「ツートップ体制」のもと、平林新社長は同氏と緊密に連携しながら経営の舵取りを担う。一方で、今年2月には筆頭株主が八木通商からアクティビストとして知られる英アセット・バリュー・インベスターズに異動。同社を取り巻く視線は一段と厳しさを増している。再建から「持続的な成長」へとフェーズが変わるなか、平林新社長は三陽商会をどのようなヴィジョンで導き、成長軌道に乗せていくのか。 ■平林義規1963年生まれ、愛知県一宮市出身。慶應義塾大学 商学部を卒業し、1986年に三井物産に入社。三井物産モスクワ有限会社への出向から本社に戻ってからは、三井物産の執行役員流通事業本部長、専務執行役員人事総務部長、顧問といった要職を歴任。2025年に三陽商会の社外取締役に就任した。2026年5月から現職。大学時代にハンドボール日本代表に選出され、現在は日本ハンドボール協会副会長を務めるほか、マスターズリーグの選手としてプレー。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: HEAD and PHANTACI Redefine Court Culture With New Street Luxe Collection
summary:
Summary

HEAD and PHANTACI have officially announced a collaborative tennis and streetwear collection arriving this SeptemberThe design integrates a signature paisley motif inspired by the fluid trajectory of a tennis shotThe range combines HEAD performance technology with PHANTACI’s signature black-and-pink color palette

HEAD and Jay Chou's PHANTACI have officially unveiled their upcoming HEAD x PHANTACI Limited-Edition Collection. Bridging professional tennis innovation with contemporary street style, the capsule translates court performance into an elevated fashion context.Rooted in HEAD’s sporting heritage and influenced by PHANTACI’s "Street Luxe" design philosophy, the collection reinterprets traditional tennis apparel. The design team drew visual inspiration from the movement of competitive play, converting the curved path of a shot into a custom paisley pattern integrated across the range.The color story centers on PHANTACI’s recognizable black-and-pink palette, bringing a modern streetwear finish to classic athletic silhouettes. Engineered with HEAD performance fabrications and infused with PHANTACI’s "Never Give Up" design ethos, each piece is built for movement on the court while functioning as a lifestyle staple beyond it.The HEAD x PHANTACI limited-edition collection will release this month.

title: sacai TO GO Lands in Paris With Exclusive Pieces
summary:
Summary

sacai is staging a limited-time pop-up called "sacai TO GO" inside Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche as part of SUPER JAPONThe space carries exclusive merchandise spanning collaborative tees, repurposed-fabric totes, plush charms and a magnetic paper-doll setCo-curated by colette co-founder Sarah Andelman, the takeover pulls in Japanese confectioners, Paris coffee shops and a rotating cast of the label's friends

sacai is bringing an immersive slice of its world to Paris with "sacai TO GO," a limited-time event on the second floor of Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche. Running as part of the store's SUPER JAPON program, the takeover blends Japanese culture with Parisian creativity across food, drink and a deep bench of exclusive merchandise.The exclusive apparel spans a run of black and white T-shirts, some carrying the sacai logo, others leaning on MA-1-inspired detailing or rocky's matcha's tiger graphic. Rounding out the shirt selection are pieces pulled from sacai's collaborations with Carhartt WIP and Nike, folding two of the label's marquee tie-ups into the same exclusive rack.Beyond the tees, the accessories carry real weight. sacai is stocking tote bags from its signature Zantan series, each crafted from repurposed archive fabrics, and pairing them with Peloqoon's plush key charms designed by plush artist Madoka Morikawa. The most unexpected object is a boxed RYVDOLL set made with French artist Ryvka Adda, a collection of magnetic paper dolls that recreate sacai's 26AW looks and let visitors mix and match styling combinations by hand.The consumables are just as considered. Toraya, a Japanese confectioner with five centuries of history, and rocky's matcha, founded by Rocky Xu, are featured throughout the run. Weekends add a rotating cast of Paris-based friends of the label, with ice cream shop F.O.L.D.E.R.O.L, bento brand Iné, kissaten-inspired sandwich and coffee spot Benchy, seasonal-cuisine specialist NIWA and coffee shop Dreamin' Man each taking a turn across the calendar.Tying the whole thing together is co-curator Sarah Andelman, co-founder and former Creative Director of the influential Paris concept store colette, who assembled a community of longtime collaborators to shape the space. The result reads as a hybrid environment, one that fuses Japanese sensibility with a distinctly Parisian creative spirit while staying unmistakably sacai.sacai TO GO is open now at Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche, running through October 11.Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche24 Rue de Sèvres, 75007Paris

title: côte&ciel Launches Transformative Bags and Accessories for FW26
summary:
The côte&ciel Fall/Winter 2026 Collection explores fashion as an active verb - an act of making, shaping, and constructing - rather than a static statement of style.Led by designer Emilie Arnault, the seasonal concept takes inspiration from Charles Fréger's photographic study Wilder Mann, which observes European folk festival costumes blending human and animal forms. This ritualistic connection to nature translates into an earthy, tactile palette that features wool-like Tweed Anthracite, home upholstery-inspired Black & Cream Tweed, lightweight Smooth Burgundy Nylon and technical Carbon Black textiles. To emphasize the craftsmanship behind the designs, the brand paired its industrial lookbook with handcrafted artistic works by Paris-based creative Aurélie Mathigot.Rooted in the philosophy of "the same song, but different instruments," the seasonal range evolves côte&ciel's iconic silhouettes through fluid, body-responsive forms that bridge the gap between bags and wearable garments. Key styles in the range include the ELVO backpack in Carbon Black, which expands and compresses to fit tech devices up to 16 inches, and the RENO shoulder bag, which unfolds into a wearable vest complete with an integrated Smooth Black hood.Furthering the origami-like construction, the compact PO S twists water-repellent nylon to transition seamlessly between a sling and a vest. The collection is completed by small accessories ("Petits Accessories"), including the AÓOS NANO pouch, eyewear cases, and modular leather charm cords like the LETGO series. The collection is available now globally through côte&ciel and will also be stocked by HBX starting September 2, 2025.

title: UNDERCOVER Turns Its ‘UNDERMAN’ Mythology Into a Feature Film With ‘UNDERGIRL’
summary:
Summary

UNDERCOVER is releasing UNDERGIRL, described as the first film from its UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION armThe story picks up the world of UNDERMAN, the art book tied to the label's 2011 spring/summer collection, and follows a hero's daughter stepping into his roleA limited Shibuya screening run brings the roughly hour-long feature to audiences this September

UNDERCOVER is stepping into filmmaking with UNDERGIRL, billed as the debut movie from UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION. The project revives the fictional universe first laid out in UNDERMAN, the photo-and-graphic art book that accompanied the brand's Spring/Summer 2011 collection, and reanimates it 15 years later as a 54-minute feature.The narrative centers on Yuri Ibuki, the daughter of a hero named UNDERMAN who has long shouldered the sorrows of the city while protecting its people. When he vanishes without warning, a mysterious envoy called Kiko appears before Yuri and guides her toward an inescapable destiny: succeeding her father and becoming UNDERGIRL. The film follows her through the trials that transformation demands.The production is led by UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION, a unit built around Jun Takahashi alongside Tetsuya Nagato, Katsuhide Morimoto and Taro Mizutani. Morimoto, a photographer and filmmaker, directs, while the screenplay was written jointly by Takahashi, Nagato, Morimoto and Mizutani. Takahashi additionally serves as executive producer.The casting anchors the fiction with recognizable faces. Sena Nakajima plays the lead, Yuri Ibuki and UNDERGIRL, opposite Ryuhei Matsuda as UNDERMAN. Kiko Mizuhara, who appeared in the original 2011 UNDERMAN project, returns here, and Mitsuko Baisho joins as another key figure moving through the story.UNDERGIRL screens at SPACE PART 3 by PARCO in Shibuya from September 14 through September 20, 2026, with weekday showings at 6 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. and weekend showings at 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. Tickets are available from September 2 via the venue's dedicated web page.SPACE PART 3 by PARCO7th floor, Shibuya Miba BuildingTokyo

title: Take an Inside Look at ‘Dressing Up,’ Sandy Liang’s First Rizzoli Monograph
summary:
Summary

Sandy Liang is releasing Dressing Up: Sandy Liang, a monograph gathering ten years of the label's visual world through Rizzoli New YorkThe book leans on previously unpublished personal photography to trace her runway moments, inspirations and take on uniform dressingCreative director Ava Nirui and stylist Dean DiCriscio contribute to the project alongside Liang

Sandy Liang is giving readers a look behind the curtain with Dressing Up: Sandy Liang, a new monograph arriving via Rizzoli New York. Marking more than a decade of her namesake label, the book compiles an intimate selection of ephemera from the designer's world and opens up the process behind the girlish, nostalgia-driven universe she has built.As an object, the release is a substantial one. It runs 276 pages in hardcover, and the interior is anchored by previously unpublished material, including personal film and iPhone photographs that Liang has kept as her own running record. Rather than a straight lookbook, the pages are curated through a close, personal lens, surfacing the inspirations, runway moments and evolving ideas around uniform dressing that have defined her output."I've been documenting my life through photos since high school when I got my first iPhone. Holding memories through photos has always felt as precious as keeping a childhood memento," Liang said in the announcement. "Sharing my life through my work feels intuitive for me - one does not feel complete without the other. This scrapbook of memories captures a decade of the brand through that lens."The visual language the book catalogs is instantly legible to anyone who has followed the label. Liang's collections have long trafficked in bows, Peter Pan collars, pleated skirts, ballet references, florals and kawaii touches, fusing a downtown New York attitude with cues pulled from memory, nostalgia and youth culture. A native New Yorker whose work draws heavily on growing up in Chinatown, she has turned that specific blend of femininity and intergenerational influence into a devoted global following, positioning the monograph as both a personal archive and a broader statement on her place in contemporary fashion.The book features contributions from Ava Nirui, the New York creative director known for her work on Heaven by Marc Jacobs, and Dean DiCriscio, a stylist who splits his time between New York and Los Angeles. Beyond documenting Liang's decade, the project is framed as an invitation, meant to encourage anyone drawn to fashion, image-making and dressing up to go build a visual world of their own.Dressing Up: Sandy Liang is available to pre-order now ahead of its September 22 release through Rizzoli.

title: BEAMS x The North Face Purple Label Flip a Down Jacket From Trail to Tarmac
summary:
Summary

BEAMS has cut a special-order reversible down jacket with The North Face Purple Label that reads as two garments in oneOne side plays up stitched, sporty down paneling while the reverse takes on a cleaner flight-jacket silhouetteThe exclusive lands in "Greige" and "Navy," both carrying the same dual-purpose build

BEAMS and The North Face Purple Label have joined on a special-order Reversible Down Jacket that packs two distinct looks into a single shell. Designed to be worn either way out, the piece swaps between an outdoor-leaning down face and a trimmer, more tailored one depending on how it is turned.The construction is the entire pitch. One face is worked with pronounced quilting stitches for a sportier, technical down look, while flipping it inside out reveals a minimal surface cut closer to a flight jacket, giving the wearer two silhouettes to move between as the outfit or mood calls for it.That versatility is backed by a layered material makeup. The shell is built from full polyester, the reverse pairs nylon with cotton, and the loft comes from a down-led fill blended with rayon and feather. Trim details are specced separately, with a nylon collar and cuffs and hem reinforced with a nylon base and traces of polyurethane for stretch and recovery.The jacket sits within The North Face Purple Label, the long-running line that pairs the outdoor giant with Japanese label nanamica, a collaboration known for reworking technical mountain staples into softer, city-ready cuts. BEAMS' special-order treatment extends that logic, taking an already design-forward platform and adding a reversible twist unique to the retailer.Both colorways, "Greige" and "Navy," are offered across a full S through XL size run, each delivering the same two-in-one functionality rather than splitting the concept between finishes.The BEAMS x The North Face Purple Label Reversible Down Jacket is available to pre-order now through BEAMS, with deliveries expected in early November 2026.

title: Poetry Distilled Into Glass: Aēsop Rewrites Its Olfactory Legacy With the Fragrant Fables Collection
summary:
Summary

Aēsop unveils its Fragrant Fables Collection, merging botanical mastery with literary allegories.New scent "Unforeseen Aer" explores imperfection via nutmeg and a “Pure Air” accord.Bottles are redesigned with amber glass and features basalt-textured caps, removable atomizers and custom-printed poem packaging.

Aēsop merges its mastery of botanical extracts with a long-standing reverence for literature to unveil the Fragrant Fables Collection, bridging two decades of personal fragrance creation since the launch of "Marrakech." Drawing inspiration from its namesake, the ancient Greek fabulist, the Australian brand has reimagined its signature range into fable-like allegories that pair philosophical questions with complex olfactory structures.Each composition is built around a dual framework: a "Radical Ingredient" - a singular, unfiltered botanical extract that reveals surprising facets - and a "Fabulist Accord," designed to evoke intangible or unscented elements in nature. Renowned favorites like "Tacit" return as "Tacit Truths," exploring trust through crisp basil and a "First Light" yuzu-fennel accord. Meanwhile, “Eidesis” transforms into "Evoking Eidesis," contrasting grounding sandalwood against a shimmering "Mirror" accord and "Aurner" debuts as "Entirely Aurner," a bold celebration of nonconformity that layers herbaceous magnolia leaf over an iridescent "Silver Ore" base.At the center of this release is a brand-new scent, the "Unforeseen Aer," an eau de parfum that poses the central philosophical question: How can change enrich us? Inspired by a fable of a gentle wind learning to embrace the sublime chaos of its own wild gusts, the fragrance offers a nonconformist take on the classic fougère family. The composition opens with a crisp, elevated "Pure Air" Fabulist Accord composed of geranium, lavandin and rosemary, evoking alpine winds rushing across rugged, uncharted heights. This airy, pristine freshness is juxtaposed against the Radical Ingredient of nutmeg, which injects a textured, spicy warmth that celebrates the beauty found within moments of imperfection. The resulting aroma is energizing yet deeply grounded, wrapping the wearer in a mood of quiet contemplation and adventurous momentum.To complete this literary and design narrative, the collection introduces an elevated iteration of Aesop's iconic amber glass bottle. The vessel features a taller form with a domed base, stamped with metallic amber typography, an embossed glass insignia and a tactile cap inspired by the basalt rock indigenous to Melbourne. Enhancing its sustainability, the bottle is equipped with an easily removable atomizer for streamlined recycling. Each fragrance is housed in a box printed with its corresponding fable-like poem, inviting a quiet moment of reflection before application.Other fragrances in the collection, such as "Eternal Karst," "Above Us, Steorra" and "Rozū Arises," continue Aēsop’s tradition of pairing botanical complexity with philosophical inquiry. Together, they form a constellation of scents that provoke thought as much as sensation, with the first phase available this month via Aēsop stores and the official website, while the remainder will follow in February 2027.

title: Acqua di Parma Expands Signatures of the Sun Lineup With “Cedro Virtuoso”
summary:
Summary

Acqua di Parma celebrates 110 years with "Cedro Virtuoso" Eau de Parfum.Crafted by Fabrice Pellegrin, it blends cedarwood and hazelnut with bergamot brightness.The 110th-anniversary release includes arrives in clear glass bottles, complete home candles, diffusers and body care.

Acqua di Parma marks its 110th anniversary with the unveiling of "Cedro Virtuoso" , a luminous new Eau de Parfum expanding the celebrated Signatures of the Sun collection.The fragrance celebrates the sensorial warmth of the creative process — translating the exact moment an intuitive spark evolves into pure, emotional expression. Designed by Master Perfumer Fabrice Pellegrin, the scent centers around a tailor-made co-infusion of dry Virginia cedarwood and rich hazelnut, macerated together side-by-side for 30 days.Opening with a sparkling lift of Calabrian bergamot, the composition transitions into a creamy, woody-gourmand heart where hazelnut’s soft, rounded warmth gently tames the balsamic, structured facets of cedarwood. The result is an enveloping, introspective trail that encourages inner confidence and evokes a feeling of effortless, contemporary elegance on skin.The olfactory narrative comes to life through a design aesthetic rooted in Italian craftsmanship and architectural purity. Housed in the iconic Signatures of the Sun clear glass bottle, the warm, golden liquid shines through like a prism of light, topped with a sleek black cap and finished with a understated black and white label.To reflect the dialogue between human touch and raw materials, the campaign unfolds inside a sunlit design atelier featuring handcrafted, sculptural cedar totems that echo the soft, rounded forms of the scent profile. The launch extends beyond personal fragrance into a complete body and home ritual, offering a body cream, hand and body wash, scented candle and room diffuser to seamlessly integrate this warm atmosphere into daily life.The "Cedro Virtuoso" Eau de Parfum is offered in multiple sizes, spanning 12ml, 50ml, 100ml and 180ml. The new scent, alongside the wider Signatures of the Sun collection is avlaiable via Acqua di Parma boutiques, select global retailers and online.

title: Fakemink and Skepta's First Collaboration Is in the New Stone Island Campaign
summary:
Stone Island's "Community as a Form of Research" remains a core part of the label's brand ethos. The recurring visual campaign platforms tastemakers across different disciplines who not only remain relevant in the zeitgeist, but actively contribute to the cultural dialogue. This past year, Stone Island has tapped a star-studded cast of talent to lead the monthly campaign, ranging from A.G. Cook and Feid, to Charlie Hunnam Chito Vera, and Breanna Stewart. For the latest installment of "Community as a Form of Research," Stone Island has enlisted the likes of some of the most timely faces, including fakemink, Skepta, and Stephen Graham.3House, Samir Bantal, Monika Sprüth and Jia Zhang-Ke also appear in the campaign. From musicians to art dealers, the six members of the campaign each offer what Stone Island calls "a distinct perspective to the broader cultural conversation that informs the brand's continuing research." As per usual, each individual is photographed in Stone Island garb styled by Max Pearmain, and answers a series of questions curated by Hans Ulrich Obrist, which selects from the questionnaire listed down the side.mink dons a bright orange hooded jacket (Q100027 SLICK NYLON TELA-TC_STONE ISLAND), made from textured nylon tela and manually treated with resin brushed over the entire surface before being heat-pressed for its glossy appearance. Similarly, Skepta also wears a hooded jacket (4100035 DENSE OXFORD NYLON-TC_STONE ISLAND), but his is crafted fully from heavyweight nylon oxford, complete with PrimaLoft®-TC quilted lining on the interior.Graham picks from the camouflage-inspired, fully monochromatic Ghost Collection, opting for the 0100004 BONDED RUBBERISED LEATHER_STONE ISLAND GHOST, a lambskin coach's jacket with a sprayed, rubberized finish. Japanese musician 3House wears a lightweight tela jacket (Q100031 HAND PAINTED DAVID LIGHT-TC_STONE ISLAND) crafted from Japanese polyester and polyamide yarns, the byproduct of an artisanal design process; each jacket is one-of-one, hand-dyed with careful heat application to shape the structure and manually painted.Take a closer look at the pieces in Stone Island's new "Community as a Form of Research" below, and find the full cast's portraits in the gallery above.
