title: NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE and Jordan Brand Launch Collaboration, Reinvigorating Athletic Heritage Through Tokyo Craftsmanship
summary:
The NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE x Jordan Brand apparel collection is officially arriving to unite Japanese craft with global athletic heritage. In an exclusive interview with Hypebeast, co-founders Masako Noguchi and Takuma Sasaki opened up about translating their 20-year legacy of refined Tokyo textile design onto an international stage.Rather than focusing on the basketball court, the project draws deep inspiration from Japan's national reverence for baseball. Building on a domestic activation alongside the Tokyo Giants from earlier this summer, the partnership centers around the story of a fictional athletic team named "RHYTHM." The apparel line avoids standard athletic mesh, opting instead for dark, wash-treated woven fabrics across structured baseball shirts and utility trousers designed to age naturally.The undisputed centerpiece of the collection is the "RHYTHM" team bomber jacket, which brings the fictional team narrative to life through embroidered floral motifs, graphic appliqués, and a detailed printed lining. The collection also highlights NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE's signature "Draw Your Garden" motif, fusing their hand-drawn floral pattern directly with Jordan Brand's iconic red Jumpman logo across a lightweight bandana. Speaking on the creative process with Hypebeast, the founders emphasized that preserving their intricate craftsmanship while executing at a global scale was paramount throughout the partnership.Hypebeast: Taking NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE from a revered, niche Tokyo label to a global platform alongside Jordan Brand is a massive milestone. Going back to your roots, what are your core personal memories associated with Jordan Brand, and does this collaboration feel like a "dream come true" moment for you both?Takuma Sasaki: My first pair of Jordans was the AJ6, which I got when I was 14. I remember how special it felt—almost like owning a piece of the culture itself.Masako Noguchi: It’s a great honor, and incredibly exciting, for us to be working with Jordan Brand on a global project.How did you navigate the design process of balancing classic sportswear structures with your signature utilitarian touch?MN: We saw our role as creating a bridge between sports and fashion. We wanted to bring our core values of textiles and craftsmanship into the collection, while creating pieces that people would genuinely want to wear on the street.Baseball holds a profoundly special place in Japanese culture, acting as a pillar of both community and national identity. As a Tokyo-based brand, how deeply does this cultural reverence for the sport resonate with you personally, and did that domestic love for baseball influence your decision to anchor a Jordan Brand collaboration around the diamond rather than the basketball court?MN: Baseball is a sport that is deeply familiar to Japanese people. When I was growing up, I remember watching baseball on television with my family almost every night.TS: In fact, in July, Jordan Brand and the Tokyo Giants presented a special project in Tokyo, featuring a collection that incorporated our signature “Draw Your Garden” print. All of the players wore the full collection during three games at Tokyo Dome. The stadium was packed with fans, and the energy was incredible. It was a very special experience for us.What makes the NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE × Jordan Brand collaboration particularly exciting is how the story carries over from one project to the next, while expanding onto an even more global stage.The collection utilizes a very deliberate, restrained black palette, accented only by the iconic red Jumpman logo. Was this intentional to allow the intricate white stitching, the co-branding on the pockets, and the handcrafted visual treatments to emerge and age beautifully over time?TS: We chose black as a key color throughout the collection, drawing on the strong association we have with Jordan. We also applied wash treatments to the garments to bring out a sense of texture and character in the fabrics, while making them feel immediately natural and comfortable on the body.One of the things we cared about most was making sure the details could be appreciated the moment you picked up a piece. We wanted to bring multiple techniques and details together within a single garment, while still allowing each element to be felt and seen.Your hand-drawn patterns and floral paisley motifs are the lifeblood of NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE. Seeing that classic floral paisley combined with the red Jumpman on the bandana is a striking visual. What is the process of taking such deeply personal, hand-drawn motifs and fusing them with one of the most recognizable logos in the world?MN: Over the 20 years since we founded the brand, we’ve created countless textile designs, but “Draw Your Garden,” our signature bandana print, is perhaps the design that means the most to us. It has become a defining part of our brand, carrying a significance almost equal to that of our logo. Including the bandana print in this collection and combining it with the Jumpman was an idea we had from the very beginning. It’s incredibly rewarding to see a single piece of fabric transformed into something so powerful and iconic.The bomber jacket acts as the undisputed centerpiece of this release. It really highlights your textile-first approach through embroidered floral motifs, graphic appliqués, and a beautiful printed lining. Can you walk us through the intricate construction of this specific piece and the story behind it?MN: During our kickoff meeting with the Jordan team, the idea came up to create a uniform for a fictional team called “RHYTHM.”The moment the idea came up, the story of the collection fell into place. We could immediately envision the product lineup and even the film. This jacket brings together everything that the fictional team “RHYTHM” represents.You've worked on various projects and collaborations over the years, but the scale of Jordan Brand is unique. How did the creative process and partnership with the Jordan team compare to your past collaborators, particularly when it came to preserving your intricate craftsmanship at a global production scale?TS: The Jordan team had actually been visiting our collections in Tokyo and Paris and getting to know our work well before this project officially began. We had already spent a lot of time talking and exchanging ideas. Our approach to collaboration has always been the same. As with our other collaborators, we take the time to have meaningful conversations before a project begins, building a deeper understanding of one another throughout the process. The Jordan team understood what lies at the heart of NOMARHYTHM TEXTILE —textiles and craftsmanship—and, importantly, how we work with those elements and bring them into a contemporary context. I think that was extremely important. We’re very grateful for the trust they placed in us, and for how thoroughly they worked through every detail, testing and refining things again and again. Collaboration is ultimately about teamwork.This collection reflects a shared belief in creative expression and the pursuit of greatness. Now that you have brought your distinct Tokyo-crafted perspective to an international audience, how do you see this collaboration impacting the future trajectory and creative ambitions of NÒMARHYTHM TEXTILE?MN: To better understand Jordan Brand, we visited the campus, where we had the opportunity to explore its historical archives and materials.It was fascinating from both a design and historical research perspective, but what resonated with us most was the brand’s open-mindedness and willingness to embrace challenges. That spirit is something we’ve always believed in and aspired to embody, and it’s something we hope to carry forward into the future. title: 「防災は人生を丸ごとハッピーにするため」　防災士・古島真子が説く“十人十色”の備え
summary: 本日9月1日は防災の日。熊本地震や各地で相次いだ豪雨被害を受け、改めて災害への備えの重要性を感じた人も多いのではないでしょうか。ただ、重要性は分かっていても、忙しい日々の中で後回しにしてしまったり、何から始めればいいのか分からなかったり──。そんな防災を、自分らしく、無理なく続けられるものに変えようとしているのが、防災士の古島真子さんです。繊維商社出身でファッション業界とも縁が深い古島さんは、「十人十色のカラフル防災」を掲げ、2024年に防災専門会社ColorfulBosaiCreationを設立。防災を“正しく備えなければならないもの”ではなく、“人生をハッピーにするための手段”と捉える古島さんに話を聞きました。 古島真子（まこぴ）／ColorfulBosaiCreation代表1990年生まれ、東京都出身。2014年にお茶の水女子大学グローバル文化学環を卒業後、繊維商社のモリリンに入社。その後、デロイト・トーマツ・コンサルティングを経て、2022年から一般社団法人unistepsでジャパンサステナブルファッションアライアンスの事務局を担当（現在も継続）。並行して、防災スタートアップのソネリスでも勤務。2024年に株式会社ColorfulBosaiCreationを立ち上げた。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: Carlos Alcaraz Took the US Open Court in New Travis Scott Nikes. Then, Travis Scott Dropped a Full "Cactus Court" Collection.
summary:
As Cactus Jack continues to align itself closer with the sports world, Travis Scott obviously had to get in on the US Open this year in some capacity. What better way than to lock back in with his longtime friend and seasoned Cactus Jack collaborator Carlos Alcaraz for his surprise return to the court?This morning, just hours before his first match since April, a new advertisement surfaced as a collaboration post on Nike and Travis Scott's Instagram pages, commemorating Alcaraz's comeback to Flushing Meadows–Corona Park. In the video, the tennis player and the rapper banter back and forth, both donning head-to-toe unreleased Cactus Jack x Nike.Alcaraz then stepped into Arthur Ashe Stadium in that same outfit he's seen wearing in the campaign video, formally debuting the new Zoom Vapor 12 HC sneaker in a Pale Ivory/Cacao colorway, paired with a matching monochromatic Cactus Jack x Nike full set. Scott sat in the stands to cheer Alcaraz on during the match against Roman Safiullin, the rapper flexing the same blue look he wore in the visual, including the long-awaited Cactus Jack x Nike Air Force 1 Low in Ice Blue. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nike (@nike) After Alcaraz's big win, Scott joined him for a victory lap, revealing the full Cactus Jack x Nike collaborative range, billed the "Cactus Court" collection. The drop spans new footwear, apparel and a New York City "Cactus Court Pro Shop" pop-up store, already up and running in the Lower East Side.Leading the drop is the Cactus Jack x Nike Air Force 1 Low landing in Ice Blue, a colorway that has been eyed long before this morning's ad, and ever since La Flame first brought 'em out at Nike Toma in Atlanta. Scott's ice blue "Cactus Court" pullover is also available for purchase, along with an earthy Cactus Court Pro Shop lightweight jacket, and Alcaraz-inspired graphicwear.Visit the Cactus Court Pro Shop now at the below address, where the Cactus Jack x Nike Air Force 1 Low is available in limited quantities.Cactus Court Pro Shop47 Chrystie StMonday: until 6 PMTuesday – Friday: 11 AM – 6 PM

title: The Met Cancels John Galliano Exhibition
summary:
SummaryThe Met canceled its Spring 2026 John Galliano exhibition due to backlash over his 2011 racist remarks.Galliano, Anna Wintour, and Andrew Bolton issued a joint statement supporting the decision, with Galliano apologizing.Following the July announcement of The Met Costume Institute’s Spring 2026 show, “John Galliano: Horizons,” the museum faced widespread backlash over Galliano’s past racist remarks. No more than a month later, the New York City museum released a joint statement with Galliano, Anna Wintour, and curator Andrew Bolton saying, “Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition."John Galliano wrote an extended remark, leading with his thanks to The Met, followed by acknowledgement of the decision. "After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time," he said. "I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it."The words Galliano is referring to date back to 2011, when a video surfaced of the designer spewing racist remarks at a Paris cafe. The incident ultimately led to his firing from the Creative Director role at Dior, his ousting from his eponymous label, and legal fines amounting to 6,000 euros. The designer returned to the industry in 2014 as the Creative Director of Maison Margiela and most recently inked a deal with Zara in 2026 for a collaborative collection.The Met Costume Institute's curator in charge, Andrew Bolton, contributed to the statement, saying, “I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care. I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused." "After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed," he added.As chairperson of the highly anticipated Met Gala, a response from Anna Wintour was also included: "John's decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is. I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support."As of the time of writing, the museum has not shared official details of what the Spring 2026 exhibition will focus on instead.

title: PUMA and Scuderia Ferrari HP Weave a Red Thread Through Michael Schumacher’s Legacy
summary:
In light of the 30th anniversary of Michael Schumacher’s arrival at Scuderia Ferrari HP, PUMA has reunited with the Formula 1 team to craft a new collection that pays homage to his historic career on the tracks. The limited-edition drop arrives ahead of the Formula 1 Monza Grand Prix. Considered Scuderia Ferrari HP’s home turf, the range becomes a joint expression of the team and Schumacher, with motorsport styles incorporating iconography and inspired emblems from the iconic racing era. Exemplifying this design approach is the red racing jacket, which draws from the driver’s race suit with contrasting white stitching, a high collar and the Scuderia Ferrari logo running across each shoulder. Other pieces, including the Replica T-shirt and Replica shirt, feature more direct references to his legacy, weaving the seven stars for each of his Championship wins across the backs. To elevate the aesthetic of the garments, PUMA also releases a cap with a laurel wreath embroidered on the brim. This drops alongside a pair of red Speedcat Pro and Speedcat sneakers that offer a fitting base to the rest of the collection with their deeply rooted motorsport heritage that has been particularly prevalent in streetwear over the past few years. Before its public debut on the Formula 1 Monza Grand Prix grid, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc sport the collection in a new campaign. Shot at the team’s garage, the visuals show how Schumacher’s influence lives on in the team today, with each piece celebrating his drive, discipline and commitment to Scuderia Ferrari HP. Shop the new PUMA for Scuderia Ferrari HP Limited Edition Monza Collection on the brand’s website now.

title: Supreme Celebrates Larry Clark's 'Tulsa' Legacy in New FW26 Collaboration
summary:
Summary

The Supreme x Larry Clark collaboration features archival Tulsa images and exclusive new photography across graphic apparel.Standout items includes hooded varsity jackets, sequin raglan tops, a bean bag and zines.The collaboration drops September 3 globally, followed by Asia on September 5.

Supreme has officially linked up with celebrated American photographer and film director Larry Clark for a collaborative release. Continuing a creative relationship that spans over 30 years, the new release draws deeply from Clark's influential body of work. Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma in 1943, Clark spent 1962 through 1971 photographing his inner circle from an insider’s perspective, pioneering a raw, deeply personal approach to documentary photography. His seminal 1971 photobook, Tulsa, exposed the quotidian violence and self-destruction in everyday American society, going on to heavily inspire subsequent generations of autobiographical photographers - from Nan Goldin to Ryan McGinley - before Clark expanded his artistic realm with Teenage Lust (1983) and his acclaimed directorial debut Kids (1995).For FW26, Supreme and Larry Clark translate this storied photographic legacy into a focused range of graphic apparel utilizing original imagery from Tulsa alongside new photographs shot exclusively for Supreme. Leading the wearable offerings is a Hooded Varsity Jacket decorated with full-placement archival photography. The drop continues with an eye-catching Sequin Raglan L/S Top and a cozy Zip Up Hooded Sweatshirt, while graphic t-shirt options arrive in the form of the Gun Tee and the Neighbor Tee, both highlighting Clark's candid portraiture across core seasonal colorways.Extending beyond traditional streetwear staples, the capsule incorporates a curated selection of lifestyle goods, skate hardware and printed collectibles decorated with Clark’s imagery. Highlighting the home goods selection is an oversized 42- inch-by-42-inch Bean Bag emblazoned with exclusive photography, serving as a distinct lifestyle statement piece. The collaborative drop is completed by a co-branded Skateboard deck and a 48-page collectible Zine, which comes outfitted with an exclusive poster insert showcasing Clark's visual archive.The Supreme x Larry Clark collaboration is scheduled for a global release later this week. The capsule will be available online and across physical Supreme chapter locations starting September 3. Fans located in Asia can expect the collection to land in-store and online on September 5.

title: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week
summary:
Summary

Palace Skateboard's latest drop is led by a GORE-TEXT jacket delivery in four colorwaysSportswear references run through the release with mesh team jerseys, rugby tops, and training sweatsPolartec fleeces with reflective and tri-ferg detailing round out this week's technical pieces

Palace Skateboards has unveiled its latest Fall 2026 weekly drop, and this one balances heavy technical outerwear against a run of sports-referencing pieces. Led by a GORE-TEX jacket delivery and backed by mesh team jerseys, rugby tops, and Polartec fleeces, the release leans on performance fabrications while nodding to the sportswear vocabulary Palace regularly draws from.The technical outerwear anchors the week. Palace's GORE-TEX jacket lands in four colorways, camo, black, olive, and orange, built stormproof and finished with contrasting zips, with a matching hat available alongside each. It is the drop's clear centerpiece, offering the weatherproofing that GORE-TEX is known for across a spread of makeups broad enough to cover both loud and understated tastes.The performance theme carries into the fleeces. Palace works Polartec fabric into pieces detailed with a reflective strip and Velcro tri-ferg accents, the latter a nod to the brand's Tri-Ferg logo, pairing warmth with the kind of functional touches that keep the release grounded in technical wear rather than pure fashion layering.Running alongside the technical pieces is a strong sportswear current. The drop includes mesh team jerseys finished with custom name tapes reading Wilson, Brady, Cannon, and Clarke, plus a set of Palermo-inspired and flipped rugby tops and training sweats. Together those pieces pull from football and rugby kit traditions, giving the week a jersey-and-pitch feel that plays off the more utilitarian outerwear.The collection launches Friday, September 4 at 11:00 a.m. BST for the UK, Europe, and US, followed by Saturday, September 5 at 11:00 a.m. local time for Japan, China, Korea, and Australia.

title: 'Backrooms' Is Rewriting What Horror Is Allowed to Be
summary:
Horror has always been good at monsters. What it's historically been less good at is dread without a source, the particular unease of being somewhere wrong without knowing how you got there or what, exactly, is coming for you. Backrooms fixes that, and in doing so has quietly become one of the most significant shifts in how the genre operates in years.The origins of this blockbuster is, almost, embarrassingly simple. It all started from single photograph uploaded to 4chan in 2019: an empty room, fluorescent lights, yellow wallpaper the color of old teeth, carpet that belongs in a mid-century office no one has cleaned since 1987. The caption described it as what you see when you "noclip out of reality." That image should not have produced what it did. And yet it became the seed for an entire collaborative mythology, built in comment sections and forums and YouTube videos by people who had never met, all agreeing on the rules of a place that doesn't exist.Kane Pixels, a teenager with a camera and editing software, took that mythology and turned it into a found footage series that has now been viewed hundreds of millions of times. The genius of his approach is restraint. Backrooms in his films is not loud. There are no jump scares engineered to make you spill your drink. The horror comes from fluorescent hum, from the sense of scale, from the implication of something just out of frame that has been watching for longer than you've been aware of it. It's the kind of filmmaking that understands atmosphere as a weapon.What separates Backrooms from the horror that came before it is where the anxiety lives. Traditional horror exteriorizes fear: there is a thing, the thing wants to hurt you, you run. Backrooms internalizes it. The terror is spatial and psychological, rooted in the feeling of being in a place that should be familiar but has been stripped of every marker that makes familiar spaces safe. There's no exits, no other people, no sky, no weather. Only the hum and the yellow and the sense that the geometry is slightly wrong in a way you can't quite name. Anyone who has ever woken up disoriented in an unfamiliar room at 3am knows the specific flavor of that feeling, and Backrooms has figured out how to sustain it for as long as it wants.It also changed who gets to make horror. Backrooms universe is genuinely collaborative, built by hundreds of contributors across platforms, each adding levels and rules and entities that the community absorbs or rejects collectively. No studio greenlit it. No distributor decided it was commercially viable. It exists because people found something in that photograph and couldn't stop thinking about it.That's the part the traditional industry is still trying to work out how to replicate. Backrooms didn't come from a pitch deck. It came from a feeling, specific and hard to articulate, that a single image managed to surface. Most horror dreams of that kind of resonance its entire career. Backrooms stumbled into it on an anonymous imageboard, and the genre hasn't quite caught up yet.Baclrooms is available now on Cathay Pacific‘s award-winning inflight entertainment system.

title: JENNIE’s Debut Collaboration With adidas Originals Embodies The Art Of “FUNCTIONAL GRACE”
summary:
Summary

JENNIE steps up as co-designer for her first full adidas Originals collection, titled "FUNCTIONAL GRACE," releasing September 1.Collection blends ballet inspiration with adidas heritage, led by the SUPERSTAR SQ BALLET.Apparel lineup spans track tops, wrap skirts, bodysuits, fleece hoodies, plus accessories like leg warmers and cut‑out socks.

Building on the anticipation generated by the initial teaser announcement and the official unveil of the SUPERSTAR SQ BALLET, adidas Originals and global icon JENNIE have formally revealed their full Fall/Winter 2026 collaborative collection.Marking her transition from longtime brand ambassador to true co-designer, the range is framed around the core concept of "FUNCTIONAL GRACE." The partnership reinterprets traditional adidas athletic codes through JENNIE’s distinct creative lens, taking foundational elements of classical ballet and subverting them into a surreal, futuristic vision of modern femininity. Shot against a cosmic, dreamlike backdrop under the theme "Cosmic Ballerina: Kinematics," the accompanying campaign highlights quiet confidence, fluidity and movement.At the center of the footwear lineup is the previously-revealed SUPERSTAR SQ BALLET, a dramatic redesign of the classic shell-toe that merges the heritage silhouette with the delicate form of a ballet pointe shoe. Constructed with a premium leather upper, soft lambskin lining, a squared-off toe box and customizable ribbon detailing, the shoe bridges street culture with dance performance art.The accompanying apparel collection expands this narrative through a comprehensive range of elevated wardrobe staples. Highlights include redesigned track tops and matching track pants featuring wraparound constructions, knit wrap cardigans, sheer sleeveless bodysuits, sheer leggings, wrap skirts, and polar fleece half-zip hoodies engineered for effortless layering. The assortment is rounded out by ballet-inspired accessories, including high-knit leg warmers and cut-out socks that reinforce JENNIE’s personal aesthetic throughout the collection.The complete adidas Originals by JENNIE FW26 "FUNCTIONAL GRACE" collection will officially release globally on September 1, 2026. The drop will be available through select adidas flagship stores, the adidas CONFIRMED app, online at adidas.com/JENNIE, and via select global retail partners. title: Ib Kamara Exits Off-White™
summary:
Summary

Ib Kamara and Off-White™ have mutually decided to part ways, ending a run that began when he joined the brand as a close collaborator of founder Virgil AblohBluestar Alliance, which took control of Off-White™ in September 2024, issued a statement thanking Kamara for his impact on the labelKamara leaves after steering signature moments for the house, including its first New York fashion show and the recent L/AB c/o Off-White launch

Ib Kamara and Off-White™ are parting ways, the brand confirmed from Milan, drawing a close to the designer's time leading the house the late Virgil Abloh built. The split was described as a mutual decision, ending a tenure that traced back to Kamara's early work alongside Abloh before he was formalized into the role in the Spring of 2022.The announcement came with a statement from Joey Gabbay, chief executive officer of Bluestar Alliance, the group that took control of Off-White in September 2024. "We are deeply grateful for Ib's vision, creativity, and the remarkable energy he brought to Off-White throughout his tenure," Gabbay said via WWD. "Ib's contributions have been instrumental in shaping and evolving the brand, and we sincerely thank him for his dedication and lasting impact."Before he ever held a title at the house, Kamara belonged to Abloh's inner circle, and he carried that closeness into the work once he took charge. His tenure produced several high-visibility moments; Kamara debuted Off-White™'s first New York fashion show in September 2024, staging it on the community basketball courts of Brooklyn Bridge Park in front of a crowd that included Flavor Flav, Camila Cabello, Leon Bridges, Suni Lee, Lena Waithe, Issa Rae, Paris Jackson, Zayn Malik, Victoria Monét and Mary J. Blige. More recently, the brand rolled out L/AB c/o Off-White, a younger and more affordable line that revisited Abloh's Off-White For All idea with a cast of musicians, models and creators.Kamara has also been building beyond the house. In June 2025 he launched Raw Materials by Ib Kamara, a 360 creative agency, extending his work past the brand he has anchored for the past few years.Off-White™ has not named a successor, and neither the brand nor Kamara has detailed what the change means for its upcoming collections.

title: JOURNAL STANDARD relume Rebuilds the Barbour Solway Zipper With Non-Oiled Cotton-Nylon and a Drawcord Hem
summary:
Summary

JOURNAL STANDARD relume has reworked Barbour's Solway Zipper as a special-order jacket built around three specific construction changesThe exclusive swaps the original waxed shell for a non-oiled cotton-nylon blend and trims the length into a relaxed mid-cut with the waist belt removedA newly added hem drawcord lets the wearer cinch a rounded shape, and the jacket arrives in Black, Natural and Khaki

JOURNAL STANDARD relume has reengineered the Barbour Solway Zipper into a special-order jacket that reworks the archive piece from the fabric up. Rather than a straight reissue, the relume version, dubbed the Solway Zipper Modify, targets three parts of the original's build to move it toward daily city wear.The most significant change is the shell. relume swaps the original's waxed construction for a non-oiled cotton-nylon blend, a high-density weave that reads lighter on the body and skips the tackiness of a traditional oiled finish. The result is a jacket that can be worn on a packed train or in a car seat without the upkeep and transfer that come with waxed cotton. The mix runs 75 cotton and 25% nylon on the outer, with a full cotton lining and a cotton collar.The cut is the second focus. relume drops the original's longer line and its waist belt, resizing the jacket into a mid-length that sits just past the hip. The looser proportion is built to layer, clearing enough room to sit over a thick knit without pulling, and the shorter hem stays out of the way when seated. It reframes the Solway Zipper as an everyday outer piece rather than a structured countryside coat.The third addition is a hem drawcord. Cinching the spindle at the base pulls the silhouette into a rounder, more contemporary shape, giving the wearer control over how boxy or tapered the jacket sits. Together the three moves shift the piece toward a relaxed, adjustable fit.The heritage detailing survives the overhaul. relume keeps the functional pocket layout, including a left-chest flap pocket and roomy gusseted pockets at the front. The corduroy collar fastens with a chin strap to stand up when needed, and the house-check lining shows at the cuff when the sleeves are rolled. Finish separates the three colorways: Black runs the collar in matching black for a cleaner urban read, Natural pairs a camel collar with the check lining in a lighter palette, and Khaki sets a brown collar against a classic sage green.The JOURNAL STANDARD relume x Barbour Solway Zipper Modify is available to pre-order now.

title: GEEKS RULE Presses Aiobahn's Viral “DIVA” Artwork Into a Hatsune Miku Triple-Collab T-Shirt
summary:
Summary

GEEKS RULE has teamed with Hatsune Miku and producer Aiobahn on a three-way collaboration T-shirtThe design centers on the cover artwork of Aiobahn's Vocaloid track “DIVA” (feat. Hatsune Miku), reproduced through GEEKS RULE's silkscreen printingAiobahn will appear as a DJ at GR8 on release day, with the tee also sold online by lottery

GEEKS RULE has brought together Hatsune Miku and producer Aiobahn for a triple-collaboration T-shirt built around one of the Vocaloid world's recent standout moments. The tee draws its graphic from the cover artwork of Aiobahn's “DIVA” (feat. Hatsune Miku), translating the track's visual identity into apparel through the label's silkscreen printing.To understand why this shirt exists, it helps to understand the pull of its three names. Hatsune Miku, the Crypton Future Media virtual singer launched in 2007, has spent nearly two decades as the face of Vocaloid culture, a software voice that grew into a genuine pop icon with a catalog powered by an entire community of producers. Aiobahn, a producer known within electronic and Vocaloid circles, sits squarely in that lineage, and his “DIVA” (feat. Hatsune Miku) became a talking point across both the Vocaloid scene and wider electronic-music listeners.That song's cover art is the centerpiece here. Rather than lean on a generic Miku likeness, the collaboration zeroes in on the DIVA jacket artwork, the image already tied to the track in fans' minds, and makes it the hero of the garment. GEEKS RULE leans on the precision silkscreen printing the label is known for to carry the artwork over, aiming to preserve the emotional, edgy atmosphere of the original rather than flatten it into a simple graphic tee.The release also doubles as an event, which fits GEEKS RULE's role as a hub for music-adjacent streetwear. On the August 29 drop date, Aiobahn himself will step behind the decks as a DJ inside GR8, turning the launch into a party rather than a quiet stock update. It is the kind of artist-present moment that ties the garment back to the music it celebrates.The GEEKS RULE x Hatsune Miku x Aiobahn T-shirt releases August 29, sold at GR8 and through the GEEKS RULE online store by lottery.

title: SKIMS Enlists Supreme Veteran & Lemaire Designer Duo Exits Uniqlo U in This Week's Top Fashion News
summary:
SummarySKIMS names a Supreme veteran as design chief, Authentic Brands Group acquires a majority stake in Drake’s OVO, and Uniqlo U says farewell to Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-Linh Tran.UGG debuts a capsule with Willy Chavarria, while Gunna leads Under Armour’s new P-Star collection.Gucci taps global stars, like BTS's Jin, EsDeeKid, Rico Nasty, and Shawn Mendes, for its Primavera push.SKIMS' New Chief Design Officer Spent 22 Years at SupremeKim Kardashian’s SKIMS shifted its creative strategy this week, appointing Erin Magee as the brand’s first-ever Chief Design Officer. The move followed Magee’s recent departure from legendary streetwear label Supreme, where she spent 22 years shaping its cultural dominance and visual identity. Magee, who also founded the women’s streetwear brand Mademe, takes on the responsibility of guiding SKIMS’ creative product direction as it expands its global footprint. Kardashian praised Magee’s ability to connect with audiences and push creative boundaries. Alongside Magee's appointment, SKIMS also promoted Kim Schraub to the newly minted role of Chief Brand Officer, signaling a robust structural shift for the booming shapewear empire.Christophe Lemaire & Sarah-Linh Tran Exit Uniqlo UAfter a defining 10-year run, Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-Linh Tran stepped down as the inaugural head designers of Uniqlo U. Their FW26 collection served as their final release for the Japanese retailer's design-forward sub-label. Since 2015, the duo bridged the gap between functional basics and high-end minimalism, transforming Uniqlo U into a commercial powerhouse that generated an estimated $1 billion in 2025 alone, according to Binance. While Uniqlo confirmed their departure, the retailer assured fans that the sub-label will continue. The fashion world now watches to see who will take the reins and if the brand can maintain its maison-level appeal without its foundational creative minds.Authentic Brands Group Acquires Majority Stake in Drake's OVO BrandGlobal brand management firm Authentic Brands Group acquired a 51% majority stake in October’s Very Own (OVO), the lifestyle brand co-founded by Drake. Under the new agreement, Drake retained a 44% share of the intellectual property, while Vince Holding Corp. secured the remaining 5% and stepped in as the core global apparel and retail licensee. The Toronto-based OVO team will continue to handle creative and design operations, but Vince Holding is taking over production, merchandising, and back-of-house logistics. The strategic buyout aims to scale OVO's footprint aggressively, with plans to open three new United States retail locations next year before pushing into major wholesale distribution in 2027.UGG and Willy Chavarria Announce Debut Capsule CollectionUGG and designer Willy Chavarria unveiled their debut collaborative capsule, blending Chavarria’s sharp cultural aesthetic with UGG’s signature boots. The unisex collection features five distinct footwear styles, including the Guard Boot, Biker Boot, and Hotel Chavarria Slipper, alongside a co-branded tee and socks. To launch the collection, the duo released the “UGG & KISSES” campaign, starring a heavy-hitting cast that includes Eva Longoria, Danny Trejo, Becky G, and Ivan Cornejo. Inspired by the '90s sitcom Married… with Children, the campaign reimagines familiar television tropes through Chavarria’s Mexican-American lens. The fierce yet friendly lineup drops globally on September 10, 2026.Gucci's Primavera Campaign Is a Fusion of K-Pop, UK Underground, DMV Rap & MoreDemna’s egalitarian vision for Gucci continues with the star-studded FW26 Primavera campaign. Photographed by Michal Chelbin against a rustic Italian interior, the visual push highlights a softer side of the fashion house's everyday wear. Leather and fur dominate the styling, with standout pieces like Jin’s motorsport jacket and Alex Consani’s purple sequined centerpiece dress stealing the show. The diverse international cast leans heavily into global pop culture, featuring BTS’s Jin, Shawn Mendes, Rico Nasty, NINGNING, and UK underground artist EsDeeKid. The campaign also pulls talent from the sports and film worlds, enlisting NFL legend Tom Brady alongside actors Xiao Zhan and Lee Young Ae.Under Armour Names Gunna Global Brand Ambassador and Creative Director of P-StarUnder Armour deepened its ties with hip-hop, officially appointing Grammy-nominated rapper Gunna as Global Brand Ambassador and Creative Director of P-Star. This new community-driven platform encompasses footwear and apparel, pulling design cues from Gunna’s lifestyle of travel, training, and stage performances. The debut 14-piece collection includes heavyweight tees, shorts, and American football-inspired HeatGear, all stamped with the P-Star logo. Additionally, the partnership introduces the UA Scorpio, a futuristic new sneaker utilizing UA HOVR cushioning. The silhouette drops in a hyper-limited "Gunna" colorway on August 27, 2026, ahead of a wider global rollout planned for early 2027.

title: TDR Broadens FW26 Collection With Technical Fabrics and Expert Craftsmanship
summary:
West London retailer The Garbstore has unveiled the Fall/Winter 2026 collection for its in-house label, TDR. The brainchild of founder Ian Paley, the new seasonal range expands the brand's offerings across both menswear and womenswear, drawing inspiration from decades of expertise in archived utility garments and global textile sourcing.Focusing on subtle, muted tones and intricate construction details, the latest lineup bridges the gap between British heritage and Japanese silhouettes, emphasizing functional durability and tactile quality. Outerwear highlights include the Cordura Balmacaan overcoat, available in unlined or Japanese Primaloft-insulated versions, alongside the Japanese canvas-lined Duxville Jacket with raglan sleeves and wrap-around pouch pockets.Denim and workwear continue to anchor the collection through pieces like the 11oz Hiroshima-woven denim Coverall Removed Jacket, featuring hand-distressed detailing, sun-aged dyeing, and hidden pocketing, alongside the military-inspired Jungle Repair Pant. In knitwear, TDR elevates to new heights to utilize the innovative Shima Seiki 3D knitting technology in Scotland for 100% British lambswool seamless crews, tunics, beanies, and scarves. Elsewhere, it is the Japanese cotton-wool check overshirts and signature crown chinos that complete the versatile drop.The full TDR collection is available now, with rolling releases available online and in-store at Couverture & The Garbstore over the following week.

title: CARNIVAL Brings Harajuku-Based WEEKEND SEQUEL to Bangkok for Exclusive Pop-Up
summary:
Summary

CARNIVAL hosts Tokyo’s WEEKEND SEQUEL for its first Thailand pop-up at CARNIVAL ONE BANGKOK.Features collaborative T-shirts combining CARNIVAL, WEEKEND SEQUEL, and Hiroshi Fujiwara’s fragment design branding.Runs August 29–30, 2026, at CARNIVAL ONE BANGKOK.

Leading Thai streetwear boutique CARNIVAL is bringing Harajuku-based retail concept WEEKEND SEQUEL to Thailand for the very first time through an exclusive two-day pop-up event. Founded by Yasunari Miyazaki, WEEKEND SEQUEL is a Tokyo-based project famous for its distinct rhythm — opening its physical Harajuku doors strictly on weekends to create a fleeting gathering place for product releases, street culture and community. The project is also closely associated with Hiroshi Fujiwara, founder of fragment design, whose creative presence and iconic lightning bolt insignia have become defining elements of the WEEKEND SEQUEL identity.To mark this cross-cultural connection between Tokyo and Bangkok, the collaboration debuts a special event-exclusive T-shirt collection that fuses the visual identities of CARNIVAL, WEEKEND SEQUEL, and fragment design. Designed to introduce the ephemeral, in-person spirit of Harajuku's weekend culture to Southeast Asia, the CARNIVAL x WEEKEND SEQUEL pop-up will run on August 29 - 30, 2026. The experience and limited graphic tees will be hosted at the CARNIVAL ONE BANGKOK flagship store, located in The Storeys at One Bangkok.

title: Diesel and ‘Final Fantasy XIV’ Channel a “Brave” Spirit for Their Collaborative Capsule
summary:
Summary

Diesel teams up with Final Fantasy XIV on a 27-piece "BRAVE" capsule collection.The range features graphic hoodies, character tees, washed denim sets and Mothercrystal jewelry.Launches September 16, 2026, via Tokyo pop-ups and Diesel online.

Diesel has teamed up with Square Enix's acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV for a multi-faceted project anchored in the shared philosophy of "BRAVE".Fusing fashion, gaming culture and contemporary art, the centerpiece of the project is a 27-piece capsule collection. The lineup translates rich gaming lore into streetwear staples, spanning washed denim jackets, wide-leg denim trousers, hoodies, long-sleeve tees, graphic T-shirts and silver jewelry. Design motifs draw directly from the world of Hydaelyn, featuring imagery of Azem’s Crystal, the Mothercrystal, the Grand Companies of Eorzea and iconic Scions of the Seventh Dawn characters including Y'shtola, Thancred, Alphinaud, and Estinien.Ranging in price from ¥11,000 to ¥207,900 JPY (approx. $69 - $1,302 USD), the collection kicks off on September 16, 2026, with an exclusive pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, which will offer custom job-icon embroidery services and a 30-set limited "Scions of the Seventh Dawn Complete Box". A wider release follows on October 2, 2026, via Diesel's official online store and the DIESEL SHIBUYA flagship, alongside secondary pop-ups at Hankyu Umeda in Osaka and Iwataya in Fukuoka later in the month. Coinciding with the drop, DIESEL ART GALLERY in Shibuya will host a collaborative collage art exhibition by renowned artist Kosuke Kawamura from October 2 through November 8, 2026.

title: Lee Byung-hun and Squid Game Creator Hwang Dong-hyuk Reunite for Sci-Fi Thriller ‘K.O. Club’
summary:
Summary

Lee Byung-hun is reuniting with Squid Game creator Hwang Dong-hyuk to lead the sci-fi thriller K.O. ClubThe film is Hwang's first feature in nearly ten years and centers on a near-future generational war over the ability to buy biological youthFellow Squid Game alum Park Hae-soo joins an ensemble that also includes Oh Jung-se, Cho Yeo-jeong and Kim So-jin

Lee Byung-hun is reuniting with Squid Game creator Hwang Dong-hyuk, this time on the big screen, to headline the sci-fi thriller K.O. Club. The project marks Hwang's first feature film in nearly a decade, with his production company Firstman Studio, which he runs with producer Kim Ji-yeon, confirming the casting and targeting a filming start in the first half of 2027.Lee is stepping back into Hwang's orbit after playing the Front Man across the Squid Game franchise, and he is not making the jump alone. The lineup also features Park Hae-soo, another face from the Squid Game world, alongside three actors coming into Hwang's fold for the first time: Oh Jung-se of It's Okay to Not Be Okay, Cho Yeo-jeong of Parasite and Kim So-jin of The Man Standing Next.The story trades the deadly playground of Squid Game for a dystopian near-future, but keeps the class conflict that runs through Hwang's work. In K.O. Club, wealth can purchase biological youth, and the film sets an aging elite that hoards money and power against a younger generation shut out of both. The title itself lays the premise bare: K.O. Club is shorthand for "Killing Oldmen Club," a name that names the generational war at the center of the plot.Firstman Studio made its name helping carry Squid Game to a worldwide audience and has since moved into television with the series Affairs Not the Only Secret. K.O. Club now stands as the company's return to feature production, made hand in hand with its founder.For Hwang, the film caps a period of enormous visibility. Squid Game ran for three seasons on Netflix and became one of the platform's most-watched titles anywhere, and it leaves him one of Korean entertainment's most closely tracked names as he pivots back to cinema.K.O. Club is targeting a filming start in the first half of 2027. Stay tuned for an official trailer and release date.

Following the immediate sell-out of its initial launch, this second release brings forward a newly curated series of one-of-a-kind vintage suitcases, each painstakingly restored by hand at the brand’s Hertfordshire workshop.Handcrafted using Globe-Trotter’s proprietary Vulcanised Fibreboard and reinforced with vegetable-tanned leather, the pieces are renewed using original manufacturing techniques that date back to 1897. Rather than erasing age, the restoration process carefully repairs essential hardware and structural elements while preserving the unique patina, travel stickers and historical character that make each piece a singular living archive.Notable highlights in the new drop include vibrant orange, cream, and sky-blue colorways, featuring contrasting leather straps, custom lining patterns, and original travel decals from historic airlines. Because every restored trunk is entirely unique, each piece exists as a true 1-of-1. The second drop of The Renewed Collection is available exclusively online via yhe brand's website, with Globe-Trotter set to expand the initiative later this year through "The Archive," a forthcoming release of exceptionally rare historic pieces curated directly from the brand’s heritage vaults.

title: Universal Studios Japan Drops Luffy Into ‘Jurassic Park’ for Its 25th Anniversary Merch
summary:
Summary

Universal Studios Japan is marking its 25th anniversary with a goods collection pairing hit anime franchises with the park's signature film attractionsThe lineup crosses 'ONE PIECE' with 'Jurassic Park,' 'Detective Conan' with 'Back to the Future,' and Junji Ito's Tomie with the Halloween icon Street ZombieThe range spans apparel and accessories including T-shirts, tote bags, stainless bottles, figures and mugs

Universal Studios Japan is celebrating its 25th anniversary by mashing up its most popular anime tie-ins with the film franchises that anchor the park, headlined by an ONE PIECE x Jurassic Park crossover and a Detective Conan x Back to the Future pairing. The special goods collection fuses each anime's world with a signature USJ attraction, arriving under the anniversary's "Discover U!!!" banner.The ONE PIECE design plants the Straw Hats' energy squarely inside the park's dinosaur territory. It depicts Luffy deep in the lush foliage of the Jurassic Park area, turkey leg in hand, cutting loose alongside a towering T-Rex. The result leans into the playful contrast between the anime's adventuring spirit and the attraction's dynamic, primeval setting, letting two very different worlds share one frame.The Detective Conan entry takes a more cinematic tack. Conan Edogawa and Professor Agasa appear in a design that directly homages the Back to the Future movie poster, a nod that gains extra resonance because Back to the Future returned to the park as part of the 25th-anniversary event "Universal Cars and Stars Collection." It is a crossover pitched at fans who can read both references at once, the kind of generation and franchise-spanning mashup the milestone year is built to enable.Rounding out the trio is a darker pairing aimed at the park's horror faithful. Junji Ito's celebrated horror manga Tomie is matched with Street Zombie, the emblem of USJ's Halloween Horror Night, bringing a world-renowned name in horror illustration together with the park's signature scare mascot.The merchandise itself spans everyday carry and collector pieces. Across the three collaborations, the range includes T-shirts, tote bags, stainless bottles, figures and mugs, giving fans of each franchise a mix of wearable and displayable options. Both pairings and their designs draw on long park histories: ONE PIECE has been a marquee USJ summer event since 2007, while Detective Conan, celebrating its TV anime's 30th anniversary this year, has appeared at the park since 2017 with attractions like real-escape-game experiences. Adding to the occasion, USJ says it has received congratulatory messages from original creators Eiichiro Oda and Gosho Aoyama marking the anniversary.The Universal Studios Japan 25th-anniversary collaboration goods go on sale September 9 at Studio Style.

title: Maison Margiela REPLICA’s “Lost Eden” Scent Builds a Forbidden Fruit Accord From Candied Apple, Vanilla and Smoky Oud
summary:
Summary

Maison Margiela REPLICA’s Lost Eden is a fruity-woody Eau de Parfum structured around a Forbidden Fruit AccordThe composition runs from a candied red apple top through a vanilla heart to a smoky oud baseThe scent ships in a weighted, black-lacquered Fantasies bottle in both a full 100ml size and a travel-friendly 10ml

Maison Margiela REPLICA has added “Lost Eden" to its Eau de Parfum lineup, a fruity-woody fragrance constructed around the collection's Forbidden Fruit Accord. Rather than chase a single dominant note, the scent is built as a three-part progression, moving from a liquor-like candied apple opening into a gourmand vanilla center and closing on a dark, smoky wood.The composition leads with a Candied Red Apple Accord, a juicy, almost liqueur-soaked top note that Margiela frames as the fragrance's first hit of temptation. The apple carries the opening's brightness and its slightly sweet, tart edge, setting up the Eden theme the scent is named for before the heavier materials arrive.Underneath sits a Vanilla Infusion at the heart. Positioned as the addictive, sultry middle of the pyramid, the vanilla softens the fruit and adds the gourmand warmth that keeps the composition from reading as a straight fruity scent. It functions as the bridge between the sweetness up top and the smoke below.The base is where the fragrance turns woody. A Smoky Oud Accord grounds everything with a long-lasting, smoky-woody depth, the note responsible for the fragrance's darker, more shadowed finish and its staying power on skin. Together the three accords give Lost Eden its intended contrast: gourmand sweetness pulled against an enigmatic, woody trail.The packaging is treated as part of the concept. Lost Eden belongs to the REPLICA Fantasies grouping, and its flacon wears a graduated black lacquer meant to evoke nightfall and the collection's dreamlike, imagined worlds. Fashioned in weighted glass and sealed at the neck with a deep black rope, the bottle carries the house's signature label with the brand logo rendered in a new textured silver finish, its iridescence shifting with the light. The Eau de Parfum comes in a standard 100ml/3.4 fl oz bottle and a travel-friendly 10ml/0.34 fl oz size.Maison Margiela REPLICA Lost Eden Eau de Parfum is available in 100ml and 10ml sizes via Maison Margiela Fragrances.

title: Hobonichi Techo and POTR’s "Stride" Cover Carries Your Planner and Essentials Like a Bag
summary:
Summary

The Hobonichi Techo's 2027 "Stride" cover is a collaboration with POTR, the lifestyle label rooted in Yoshida & Co.'s bag-making craftBuilt from matte, soft-touch nylon, the cover is shaped like a small bag with a removable shoulder strap so the techo can be carried hands-freeIt launches in two versions, a peacock blue A6 Original and an evergreen A5 Cousin, each with a full system of interior and exterior pockets

Hobonichi Techo has revealed "Stride," a new cover for 2027 made in collaboration with POTR, a lifestyle brand drawing on the artisanship of Yoshida & Co. Rather than treating the cover as a simple sleeve, the two have reimagined it as a compact carry piece, wrapping the planner in bonding-treated nylon and adding a removable strap so the whole thing can be slung over a shoulder like a bag.The material sets the tone. Each cover is cut from a supple nylon finished with Yoshida & Co.'s signature bonding treatment, giving it a matte surface that stays soft to the touch. That fabric expertise is the throughline of the partnership: POTR operates as a lifestyle offshoot of Yoshida & Co., the Japanese manufacturer behind the long-running PORTER label, and the "Stride" cover leans on that heritage of everyday carry goods rather than treating the techo as pure stationery.Function is where the bag concept earns its name. A front flap pocket keeps small items like earphones within reach, while a back pocket closes with a one-touch snap fastener sized for the things you grab most often. Unzip the cover and the interior opens into a considered storage layout: three card pockets and a clear pocket on the left, a zippered mesh pocket on the right, and a pen hook that takes slim pens directly or clips thicker ones. The included black shoulder strap detaches and adjusts to length, so the cover can travel closed and hands-free.The two sizes are tuned to different planners and different palettes. The A6 Original arrives in peacock blue, a refined shade meant to read as a stylish accent against any outfit, with an interior lined in navy and light gray and a single-compartment front flap pocket. The larger A5 Cousin comes in evergreen, a deep, composed green that settles easily into a workday or a day off, paired with a green-and-beige interior and a front flap divided into two sections for tidier organization. The Cousin's back pocket also runs roomier, with space for a smartphone alongside documents. A circular logo stitched to the front finishes both.Taken together, the two covers make a clear pitch to the Hobonichi faithful, a community that treats the techo less as an agenda and more as a daily companion. By building the cover to leave the house on its own, POTR and Hobonichi Techo are nudging the planner further into everyday-carry territory, somewhere between a notebook and the small bag you already reach for on the way out the door.Both "Stride" covers go on sale September 1 at 11 a.m. Japan time through the Hobonichi Techo online store.

title: New Era and Brooks Brothers Stitch the Golden Fleece Onto Buckram-Free 59FIFTY and Cross-Strap 9TWENTY Caps
summary:
Summary

New Era and Brooks Brothers have teamed on a co-branded cap collection carrying the Brooks Brothers logo and its Golden Fleece emblemThe lineup runs across two silhouettes, a structured-but-soft 59FIFTY fitted and an adjustable cross-strap 9TWENTYSix colorways span denim washes on the fitted and muted pastels on the adjustable

New Era and Brooks Brothers have joined forces on a third headwear collection that puts the American trad house's branding on two of New Era's core silhouettes. Built around the Brooks Brothers logo and its Golden Fleece emblem, the capsule is split between a 59FIFTY fitted cap and an adjustable 9TWENTY, each engineered for a softer wear than their standard counterparts.The 59FIFTY is the more construction-focused of the two. New Era has removed the inner buckram from the front panel, dropping the stiff structure that normally holds a fitted cap upright in favor of a softer, more relaxed feel against the head. Because it carries no adjuster, the fit is dialed in through sizing rather than a strap, offered in roughly 1cm increments so wearers across a wide range of head sizes can land a precise fit. The absence of a rear closure also leaves the back panel clean, giving the cap an unbroken silhouette. This version is cut from denim, with a cotton composition, and comes in two washes: Indigo Denim and Washed Denim.The 9TWENTY handles the adjustable side of the range. It uses an unstructured, coreless front for the same soft feel up top, then adds a rear cross-strap for on-the-fly sizing. Rather than a single one-size build, New Era offers it in three spans, S/M (54–58cm), M/L (57–61cm) and L/XL (61–65cm), so the strap fine-tunes an already close base size. The 9TWENTY is cotton and arrives in four muted tones: Camel, Blue Tint, Blush Sky and Lavender.Branding is the connective tissue across both silhouettes. Each cap carries the Brooks Brothers logo alongside the Golden Fleece, the house's longstanding emblem, positioning the graphics as the throughline that ties the denim fitted and the pastel adjustable into one collection. The result is a headwear range that leans on material and fit distinctions up front while using shared insignia to hold the capsule together.The New Era x Brooks Brothers cap collection is available through New Era Japan.

Authentic Brands Group has officially acquired a 51% majority stake in the intellectual property of October’s Very Own (OVO). The deal partners the global brand management platform with co-founder Drake, while tapping Vince Holding Corp. as OVO's core global apparel and retail licensee.Under the terms of the transaction, Drake retains a 44% ownership stake in the brand, while Vince Holding Corp. acquires 5% alongside the operational rights to OVO’s retail footprint. Founded in 2008 by Aubrey "Drake" Graham, Oliver El-Khatib, and Noah "40" Shebib, the Toronto-bred label currently operates 12 standalone stores across Canada, the United States, and the United Kingdom. Under the new agreement, OVO’s creative and design teams will remain based in Toronto, while Vince Holding oversees global production, merchandising, logistics, and back-of-house operations.The transaction aims to accelerate OVO’s expansion within the global streetwear market. Vince Holding plans to open three new U.S. retail locations next year before introducing OVO into major wholesale accounts starting in 2027.

title: What Is Uniqlo U Without the Lemaire Duo?
summary:
This week’s unveiling of the latest Uniqlo U range not only marks the 10th anniversary of Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-Linh Tran’s line, but also their final release as its head designers. After months of speculation, Uniqlo’s messaging around the FW26 collection has explicitly confirmed the conclusion of their direction over Uniqlo U. However, the brand also stated that “their meticulous tailoring and timeless designs will continue to live on in the next chapter of Uniqlo U,” signaling that the line has not reached the end of its life.For the last 10 years, Uniqlo U has served as the Japanese retailer’s more elevated, design-forward range, coexisting with its established main line. Binance reported that in 2025, Uniqlo U may have contributed an estimated $1 billion in annual retail sales, amounting to 5% of Uniqlo’s revenue for the fiscal year. Uniqlo U’s consistent popularity was only amplified by the accelerating growth of Lemaire. According to BoF, Lemaire’s sales grew from €10 million in 2019 to over €103 million in 2024. The relationship was mutually beneficial.In short, it was the right partnership at the right time. During the 2010s, fashion-conscious consumers began to take greater notice of quality and developed a taste for more considered minimalism amid rapid microtrends. It was the era when the “normcore” aesthetic emerged and “athleisure” evolved into a distinct category in the fashion landscape. In tandem with Uniqlo’s pared-back basics, Uniqlo U offered a meeting in the middle: a versatile balance of function and style, consistent newness executed with a timeless sensibility, and designer-approved pieces at accessible price points.But the Lemaire-powered U label wasn’t the first or only collaboration the retailer has had. The company had been perfecting its formula in the years leading up to Uniqlo U. Notably, it seemed to understand the movement toward minimalism with preceding collaborations: Jil Sander (2009), Undercover (2012), Theory (2014), and more. Shortly after a limited-edition Lemaire x Uniqlo collection in 2015, Christophe Lemaire and Sarah-Linh Tran were appointed the inaugural designers of the Uniqlo U line and the artistic directors of the company’s R&D (research and development) lab in Paris.Since then, the retailer has expanded its scope, maintaining ongoing collaborative lines with designer Jonathan Anderson, tennis player Roger Federer, and artist KAWS. Furthermore, in 2024, the company appointed Clare Waight Keller as global creative director and introduced her dedicated Uniqlo: C line. By 2025, Fast Retailing saw its Japanese revenue surpass 1 trillion yen, a first-ever for the company. While much of this can be attributed to global retail expansion, the label is also increasingly defined by its longstanding collaborators, so it's worth asking whether their departures could affect its success. With the brand saying farewell to the duo that has propped up its longest-running collaboration, what’s next for Uniqlo U?The news leaves open questions about whether the company will appoint a new designer for the U line or if it can continue successfully without a collaborative leader. The retailer has invested deeply in relationships with some of the most respected designers, and it’s the Lemaire duo who have done much of the heavy lifting for the brand over the last decade. Uniqlo stands out as a mass brand with maison-level designer affiliations, and if we can learn anything from the major fashion houses, it's that the DNA of the best creative directors remains long after their leadership concludes.

title: PHENIX's "Where's the Goddamn Horizon?" Collection Reengineers Alpine Tailoring for FW26
summary:
Summary

PHENIX unveils a Fall/Winter 2026 collection themed around the disappearance and redefinition of the horizon lineThe design language draws on film director David Lynch and a disoriented pilot's cry mid-dogfight to warp length balance, cutting, and structural seamsTechnical mountain fabrics meet urban minimalism as the label carries its 70-plus years of ski expertise into a fashion-focused line

PHENIX has unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, a lineup that takes the horizon itself as its central subject and then deliberately loses it. Presented under the label's ongoing "From Snow Mountain to the Streets" concept, the season is titled "Where's the Goddamn Horizon?" and treats the vanishing of a stable baseline as both a mood and a construction method.The theme reaches back to two reference points named in the collection's framing. One is the fascination with the aesthetics of the horizon that director David Lynch developed in his younger years. The other is the phrase shouted in the chaos of aerial combat that gives the season its name, the moment a pilot caught in a dogfight loses all sense of orientation and can no longer tell sky from ground. PHENIX takes that instant of vertigo, where the boundary between up and down collapses, and treats it as a design brief.Rather than illustrate the idea with graphics alone, the label built it into the garments. The reference line that a silhouette normally hangs from has been pushed out of its expected position, and that shift ripples through length balance, cutting, and the placement of structural seams. Coats stretch long, outerwear volumes swell and drop, and proportions land slightly off from where the eye expects them, so the clothes read with a new focal point instead of a familiar one. The looks pair heavy, protective outer layers with wide, fluid trousers, a tension between mass and drape that keeps the disorientation working across the full outfit.Underpinning the concept is the material engineering PHENIX has spent decades refining on the mountain. The collection uses WINDSTOPPER PRODUCTS by GORE-TEX LABS for its combination of wind resistance and breathability, alongside a proprietary phenix fabric that stays thin while holding up to high water pressure and remaining breathable. Down pieces appear across the range in tones spanning deep blue, burgundy, and forest green as well as black, sitting next to cable knits and tailored topcoats. Executive Creative Director Daisuke Gemma steers the design, folding the weight and comfort of high-performance snow gear into something closer to city minimalism.That mountain-to-street logic is the throughline of PHENIX's own history. The brand launched in Japan in 1952 and moved early on nylon, adopting the then-new material for ski wear by 1955 and helping set the template for the category. In 1978 it developed down capable of withstanding the ultra-high-altitude conditions of the Dhaulagiri expedition at 8,167 meters, a first for the country, and supported the climb to the summit. That track record carried into supplying athletes on Japan's Olympic national team, and as recently as the 2024 Fall/Winter season the label signed on as a supplier to Ski Team Sweden Alpine AB. More than seven decades in, this collection reframes that accumulated technical knowledge as a fashion proposition, one that finds a new landscape for clothing precisely by letting the horizon slip away.The PHENIX Fall/Winter 2026 collection opens for pre-order on August 27 through HBX and the label's online store.

Under Armour has officially appointed multi-platinum artist Gunna as Global Brand Ambassador and Creative Director of P-Star, a new creative platform spanning apparel, footwear, and community-driven storytelling. The partnership marks the next evolution of the brand’s relationship with the artist, debuting alongside an inaugural 14-piece collection and a new footwear silhouette.The debut P-Star range draws design inspiration from the rhythm of Gunna’s daily life, translating elements of training, travel, and stage performance into wearable garments. The line includes heavyweight tees, shorts, sweats, and American football-inspired HeatGear® apparel, with each item finished with an embellished P-Star logo.Headlining the initial capsule is the UA Scorpio, Gunna’s first official sneaker collaboration with the brand. Engineered with UA HOVR™ cushioning technology, the silhouette blends Under Armour’s sports performance heritage with a modern, futuristic design language. The shoe debuts in an exclusive "Gunna" colorway as a hyper-limited drop ahead of a wider release planned for early 2027.The debut P-Star collection releases on Thursday, August 27, 2026, exclusively online.

title: ファッションにも注目！プロが推す音楽シーンの次世代アイコン6選
summary: FASHIONSNAPでは、ファッションを中心とした国内の次世代クリエイターを特集中。4本目となる今回は、現代の音楽シーンとそれを取り巻くポップカルチャーを、独自の視点で捉えた文章や音声コンテンツで知られる音楽ライターのつやちゃんに、音楽性だけでなくファッションの個性も光る気鋭のミュージシャンを、ジャンルレスに推薦・寄稿してもらった。 　音楽とファッションは、いつの時代も密接に結びついている。パンクロックにおけるライダース、ヒップホップのバギーなシルエット、グランジのネルシャツ。音楽から生まれたコミュニティにはそれぞれを象徴する装いがあり、ファッションとは、どんな文化に属しているのかを伝える記号でもあった。しかし、今の若いミュージシャンたちを見ると、その関係性は変化している。「このジャンルだから、この服」という定型のスタイルよりも、目を引くのは一人一人のユニークな組み合わせだ。Y2Kやギャル、アウトドア、モード、アニメ、さらに古い時代のスタイルまで、異なる時代や地域の文化を横断し、自分の感覚で選び取っていく感性に満ちている。 　だからこそ、今、ミュージシャンの服を見るのが面白い。どんなアイテムを選び、何と何を結びつけるのか。その選択と組み合わせに、その人自身のアイデンティティや美意識が表れる。ファッションは、ジャンルやシーンへの所属を示すものから、よりパーソナルな美学を映し出すものへと広がっているのだ。本コラムでは、そんな次世代アーティストの中から、特に注目したい6名を紹介しよう。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: 【オフィス訪問レポ】ハースト婦人画報社編　自社スタジオにマッサージルームも
summary: 話題の企業のオフィスを紹介する人気連載企画「オフィス訪問レポ」。約4年ぶりに復活した今回、「エル（ELLE）」や「婦人画報」など運営するハースト婦人画報社およびハースト・デジタル・ジャパン（以下、ハースト）のオフィスを取材しました。広々としたカフェテリアや自社スタジオがあるという、移転して間もない新オフィスの気になる内側は？ 📝読む前に知っておきたい：ハースト婦人画報社およびハースト・デジタル・ジャパンとは？　ハースト婦人画報社は、世界40ヶ国で情報、サービス、メディア事業を展開するアメリカ・ハースト傘下の日本のメディア企業。ハースト・デジタル・ジャパンは、デジタルメディアやWEB事業の強化・拡大を担うために、2016年に株式会社ハースト婦人画報社の100％子会社として設立。1905年に創刊した「婦人画報」をはじめ、「エル」、「ヴァンサンカン（25ans）」、「ハーパーズ バザー（Harper’s BAZAAR）」、「エスクァイア（Esquire）」などを中心に、ファッション、ライフスタイルなどに関する多数のデジタルメディアの運営と雑誌の発行を手掛けている。Eコマース事業にも注力するほか、近年はクライアント企業のマーケティング活動のサポート事業を行うなど、コンテンツ制作における知見にデジタルとデータを融合した企業活動を行う。また、環境マネジメントシステムに関する国際規格「ISO14001」を取得しサステナビリティに配慮した経営を実践している。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: 沖田修一＆姫野花春と本屋さんへ。物語が教えてくれた「表現」の自由と面白さ
summary: 「南極料理人」で話題を集め、「横道世之介」「キツツキと雨」「さかなのこ」などを手掛けてきた映画監督 沖田修一さんの、長編映画デビュー20周年を記念したオリジナル新作映画「さとこはいつも」が9月18日に公開される。同作は、ひょんなきっかけから自分の人生を“物語”として書きはじめる、年齢も育った環境も異なる、同じ「さとこ」という名前の3人の女性たちを描いた物語。同作に登場する「さとこ」の一人で、初恋を持て余し、物語を通して妄想を暴走させていくチャーミングな中学3年生 中井聡子を演じたのは、同作が映像作品デビュー作となった16歳の若手俳優 姫野花春さんだ。 　沖田監督と姫野さんの共通点は、10代から表現活動を始めたことと、本好きであること。お互いのキャリアにとって節目となる作品を共にした2人ならば、本を通してこそ語れることがあるのでは？と、会議室を飛び出して向かったのは小さな古書店。キャリアも世代も異なる2人の、表現における原体験と「物語」から教わったこととは？ 沖田修一 （Syuichi Okita） 映画監督 1977年8月4日生まれ、埼玉県出身。短編映画の自主制作を経て、長編作品『このすばらしきせかい』（06）でデビュー。『南極料理人』(09)が大きな話題となり、2009年度新藤兼人賞金賞を受賞し国内外で高い評価を受ける。『横道世之介』(13)では、第56回ブルーリボン賞最優秀作品賞のほか、第5回TAMA映画賞最優秀作品賞などを受賞。その他の監督作品に、『キツツキと雨』（12）、『モヒカン故郷に帰る』(16)、『モリのいる場所』(18)、『おらおらでひとりいぐも』(20)、『子供はわかってあげない』（21）、『さかなのこ』(22)、ドラマ「0.5の男」(23/WOWOW)、「探偵さん、リュック開いてますよ」(26/EX)などがあり、星野源や乃木坂46のMVも手掛けている。 姫野花春 （Kashun Himeno） 俳優 2010年4月21日生まれ、京都府出身。幼少期より歌やギター、ミュージカルなどに親しみ、表現することに強い関心を抱く。「さとこはいつも」がオーディションを経ての映像作品初出演。好きな本は「海辺のカフカ」（村上春樹）。最近読んで面白かったのは「深夜高速バスに100回ぐらい乗ってわかったこと」（スズキナオ）。 このコンテンツは FASHIONSNAP が配信しています。

title: 8 Drops You Don't Want to Miss This Week
summary:
With another week upon us, we have yet another installment of our product drops series.This week’s lineup of drops kicks off with Palace Skateboards' Fall 2026 Drop 4 which is headlined by a playful Betty Boop capsule featuring chenille varsity jackets and co-branded headwear, alongside a mainline delivery focused on transitional utility like the Big Ripstop jacket. Honoring Kobe Bryant's "Mamba Mentality," FC Barcelona has debuted its striking purple and yellow "Barça Mamba" away kit adorned with a subtle snakeskin texture and an iridescent sheath logo. A24 has opened a limited-time pop-up store at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, offering vintage-style Backrooms apparel in collaboration with GEEKS RULE, logo tees for The Drama, and official film merchandise. SOPHNET. and L.L.Bean have collaborated on a highly durable 24 oz heavy canvas Boat and Tote bag, featuring SOPHNET.’s signature scorpion embroidery and a classic L.L.Bean trim tag across three versatile sizes. Blending Western aesthetics with elevated materials, WILDSIDE Yohji Yamamoto and NEEDLES have released a limited-edition S/S Cowboy One-up Shirt crafted from smooth satin and embroidered with both brands' signature butterfly and rose motifs. Stockholm Surfboard Club and RHC’s "Black Beach" special-order capsule merges Swedish surf culture with understated style, notably reimagining SSC's signature red icon tag in navy across a compact lineup of mostly black apparel. Kith’s expansive Fall 2026 collection delivers elevated outerwear and lifestyle classics, highlighted by two major standalone partnerships featuring a 30-team sueded velour NFL shirt capsule and a Western Americana-inspired debut collection with Needles. Finally, Stüssy and eYe JUNYA WATANABE MAN’s FW26 capsule masterfully blends prep-inspired classics with streetwear twists, offering fall staples like Ivy League-style blazers and Oxford shirts featuring discreet front branding and bold back graphics.Check out this week’s 8 drops you don’t want to miss below.Palace Fall 2026 Drop 4Palace Skateboards’ Fall 2026 Drop 4 is headlined by an official Betty Boop collaboration with Fleischer Studios. The playful capsule features the iconic cartoon heroine sporting a custom Tri-Ferg logo across chenille varsity jackets, fleece hoodies, woven button-downs, graphic tees, and co-branded headwear. Alongside the collaboration, Palace’s mainline delivery focuses on transitional utility. Standout items include the durable Big Ripstop jacket and jogger set, Dove Stamp waffle long-sleeves, and the coordinated Legacy collection offered in classic and woodland camo colorways. The collection releases in-store and online globally on August 28, 2026, with the Asia and Australia drop following on August 29.FC Barcelona Kobe Bryant-Inspired "Barça Mamba" Away Kit FC Barcelona has officially launched its new "Barça Mamba" away kit, debuting on the pitch against Elche CF on Kobe Bryant’s birthday. Honoring the late basketball legend and his iconic "Mamba Mentality," the striking kit features a signature purple and yellow colorway. The jersey showcases a black-to-purple gradient, while the shorts boast a subtle purple snakeskin texture. The entire kit, including the socks, is accented with an iridescent Kobe sheath logo. Rounding out the collection are a matching black and purple snakeskin track jacket and a golden-yellow snakeskin goalie jersey. The "Barça Mamba" collection is available now via FC Barcelona's webstore.A24 x GEEKS RULE Backrooms and The DramaA24 has officially opened a limited-time pop-up store at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, running through September 3, 2026. Celebrating the releases of Backrooms and The Drama, the event is headlined by an apparel collaboration with Japanese fashion brand GEEKS RULE. The standout items are a trio of 1990s-inspired, vintage-style silkscreen T-shirts featuring Backrooms' iconic "Yellow Labyrinth" imagery. Additionally, the pop-up offers official logo tees for The Drama in classic black, white, and burgundy colorways. Visitors can also shop a curated selection of A24 film soundtrack vinyl records and official studio merchandise.SOPHNET. x L.L.BeanSOPHNET. and L.L.Bean have teamed up to rework the iconic Boat and Tote bag. Retaining the functional foundation of L.L.Bean's signature carrier, the collaborative tote is constructed from highly durable 24 oz heavy canvas cotton. SOPHNET. adds its distinctive touch to the classic design with a brand-name patch and a signature scorpion embroidery, perfectly complementing the traditional L.L.Bean trim tag. Available in classic black or natural colorways, the versatile bag is offered in Large, Medium, and Mini sizes to suit various everyday needs. The SOPHNET. x L.L.Bean Boat and Tote officially releases on August 28 via SOPH. stores, dealers, and online.WILDSIDE x NEEDLES S/S Cowboy One-up ShirtWILDSIDE Yohji Yamamoto and NEEDLES have joined forces to release the collaborative S/S Cowboy One-up Shirt. Melding Western aesthetics with elevated materials, the boxy shirt is crafted from a smooth, subtle-striped satin blend finished with black snap buttons. The design highlights a literal meeting of the brands' signature motifs, featuring NEEDLES' iconic butterfly and WILDSIDE’s signature rose embroidered across the chest and back. Notably, the back rose is rendered in an exclusive purple thread for this special release. Limited to one per customer, the WILDSIDE x NEEDLES shirt officially releases on August 26 via WILDSIDE Yohji Yamamoto.Stockholm Surfboard Club x RHC "Black Beach" CollectionStockholm Surfboard Club (SSC) and RHC have partnered for the "Black Beach" special-order capsule, marking one of SSC's largest ranges to date. The exclusive collection features a significant world-first: SSC’s signature red icon tag has been reimagined in navy. The compact, predominantly black lineup includes a hooded shirt, a polo shirt, a logo cap, and a white back logo tee. Each piece is thoughtfully adorned with one of three signature SSC logos, perfectly blending Swedish surf culture with RHC’s understated style. The "Black Beach" collection is available now at RHC Ron Herman stores and releases online on August 29.Kith Fall 2026Kith has officially unveiled its expansive Fall 2026 collection, highlighted by two major standalone partnerships with Japanese label Needles and the NFL. The seasonal apparel range delivers elevated outerwear, staple knitwear, and lifestyle classics, utilizing specialized garment washes and premium leather craftsmanship across pieces like the Vintage Leather Alonzo Jacket. The collaborative offerings feature a 30-team sueded velour NFL shirt capsule and a debut Kith x Needles collection blending Japanese design with Western Americana on track jackets and fringed trousers. Following an initial accessories drop, the full Kith Fall 2026 collection releases globally on August 28 in-store and online.Stüssy x eYe JUNYA WATANABE MANStüssy and eYe JUNYA WATANABE MAN are teaming up once again to release a new Fall/Winter 2026 capsule that masterfully blends prep-inspired classics with subtle streetwear twists. Dropping on August 28, the collection features a range of versatile fall staples where discreet front branding gives way to bold back graphics. Standout pieces include an Ivy League-style blazer boasting a faded Stüssy Venus graphic on the reverse, a varsity jacket with intricate dragon embroidery, and Oxford shirts adorned with tonal chest emblems. Rounding out the lineup are understated leather and utility jackets, alongside olive ripstop cargo pants. The collaborative range will be available at Stüssy stores and Dover Street Market Ginza.

title: ‘NBA 2K27’ Announces New Updates That Will Change the Way You Play
summary:
Gaming publisher 2K is keeping excitement high for the release of NBA 2K27. Following the reveal of the new gameplay trailer, it has now shared more details about the video game’s latest features, player modes and conceptual settings, as well as all-important information on early access. The latest details were unveiled at the franchise’s first live presentation at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles. Through a 45-minute livestream, fans and gaming experts were able to experience the updates firsthand, such as the all-new Co-Op Mode. For the first time in the history of the game, this feature will let players invite a friend to their MyCAREER, creating a sense of collaboration and competition that goes beyond NBA 2K27.Another highlight from the event was the reveal of Eras. As it says in the name, the integrated timeline gives players the chance to build their MyCAREER profiles across five iconic eras in basketball history, including the Magic vs. Bird period, the Michael Jordan generation and Steph Curry’s ongoing career.After hosting the livestream, the publisher announced it would be moving the early access date two days earlier to August 26, 2026. Available to those who pre-order the Deluxe and Ultra editions, it will allow fans to trial some of the updates set to hit MyTEAM, the City, and MyCareer. Check out the new trailer above for a look at the players featured in NBA 2K27.NBA 2K27 is available to buy on September 4, 2026, with early access to the special edition beginning August 26. Head to the 2K website to find out more about how to purchase.
